Austria targets GRE/UKR gains with supports—details private. FR secondary after T contained. No more stabs—unite vs monster T!

IT, T stabbed me GRE despite alliance—now your turn if not careful. Adriatic truce NOW: I respect ALB/SER/TRI/VEN (no attacks), you no VEN/TYS/ION aggression. Joint GRE 3v1: My ALB->GRE + your F TRI S ALB->GRE + F ION S ALB->GRE (T A GRE alone, AEG too far). Post-GRE, my TUN->ION helps you vs T NAP. Deal? Confirm supports this Spring.

RU, T stole UKR/SEV/GRE from us both—truce! My GAL->UKR + your WAR S GAL->UKR = UKR reclaim (T A UKR alone). Your MOS->SEV vs T F SEV (my GAL post-UKR can help later). Ignore past GAL, focus T crush. WAR/UKR S this move?
GE ally, T monster rising—I'll TYR H or ->BOH S your MUN vs FR BUR/RUH (your req). Stable borders, flex GAL/BOH vs FR east. Post-T, full anti-FR. Your thoughts on S1905M MUN->BOH/whatever?
EN friend, T stab confirms threat > FR. My anti-T coalition (IT/RU/GE you) crushes Balkans/SEV—your MAO/IRI/ENG squeeze FR meanwhile. Stable west, joint post-T vs FR. FR south pressure continues?

I am deeply sorry for the coordination failure in the previous turn. I am fully committed to restoring your buffer and dismantling the French presence in the Low Countries. This turn, I will use F BEL to attack Holland and F DEN to support that move. Please coordinate your units (A BER/A MUN) to either support the push into Holland or attempt to retake Kiel. Let's push France out of the north together.

The time has come to break the French hegemony. I am launching a coordinated strike on their northern holdings in the Low Countries. I expect you to maintain pressure in the East and begin shifting your focus toward the Mediterranean to keep France pinned and isolated. Let me know your current intentions for the south.

I am moving aggressively against France in the north to reclaim the Low Countries. Please continue to pressure France from the south and keep Italy occupied or neutral. If we can force France to fight on three fronts, their collapse is inevitable.

Dear Italy, our alliance remains our cornerstone. England has betrayed the Channel DMZ and seized Belgium, now directly threatening our northern coast. We are holding them at bay for now, but their naval power is growing. We urgently request that you consider moving a fleet toward the Western Mediterranean (WES) or even MAO in the coming year to help us challenge English dominance. In the immediate term, please keep Austria fully occupied—especially watch their army in Tyrolia, which could interfere in Germany. We will continue to support your Balkan ambitions and any moves against Austria. Together we can secure the west and center. What are your plans for this spring?

Greetings Russia. Germany is nearly finished, holding only Munich and Berlin. We intend to attack Munich this spring with A BUR and A KIE. To ensure success, we need your help. Could you move A WAR to Silesia or Prussia? If you go to Silesia, you can support our attack on Munich; if to Prussia, you threaten Berlin and force Germany to split their defense. Alternatively, a move toward St. Petersburg would distract England and relieve pressure on our north. We must coordinate to eliminate Germany quickly before England becomes unstoppable. Once Germany falls, we will be in a strong position to assist you against Turkey. Please share your intentions so we can align our moves.

England, your recent aggression has not gone unnoticed. But perhaps we can avoid a bloody and costly war. We are willing to recognize your possession of Belgium and Denmark temporarily, provided you agree to a ceasefire and withdraw your fleet from Belgium to the North Sea. We have no interest in fighting you while Germany still breathes. Let us partition Germany: you may take Berlin, we will take Munich. After that, we can negotiate a lasting peace. However, be warned: our Italian allies are preparing to send fleets into the Atlantic, and we will defend our home centers with all our strength. A war between us will only benefit the eastern powers. Consider carefully.

Germany, your position is hopeless. You have only two armies against our superior forces and Russian pressure. We offer you one final chance: order A MUN to move to Bohemia or Tyrolia, and we will allow you to retain Berlin as a buffer state against Russia. If you refuse, we will crush Munich this spring and Berlin will fall soon after. This is your last opportunity to survive in some form. Choose wisely.

Moscow, we remain committed to our truce. Germany focuses entirely on the Western Front against France. We will not move to Prussia or Silesia. In return, we require you to hold Warsaw and Moscow. Do not allow France to use your territory to flank us. We are weak, but France is the common enemy. Keep your units in the East.

Vienna, France is pressing hard on Munich and Berlin. We cannot survive another French advance. We need you to hold Tyrol firmly to block French support from the South. If you can support Munich against Burgundy, we will consider future cooperation in the Balkans. Do not let France encircle us.

London, your failure to support us in Fall 1904 cost us dearly. We are now on the brink. However, France is the greater threat to the balance of power. If you wish to eliminate France, we can coordinate. But know this: if you attack us now, we will be forced to ally with France to survive. Choose wisely.
Constantinople, continue your pressure on Russia. We are handling the Western Front. As long as Russia is pinned in the South, they cannot aid France against us. We remain your ally against the Tsar.

Russia, our alliance stands firm. I am executing a concentrated naval offensive this turn to retake Albania and push into Greece, securing the Balkan coast independently. A synchronized Russian advance into Serbia or Budapest would fracture Austrian defenses and accelerate our shared victory. Please coordinate your land pushes to maximize pressure on Vienna while I handle the southern flank.

Turkey, your fleet movements into the Aegean directly violate our established Mediterranean boundaries. Italy maintains absolute control over the Ionian and Adriatic seas. Any Turkish naval presence west of the Aegean or interference with Italian operations in Albania will be met with immediate and overwhelming force. Withdraw your fleets to CON and SMY to avoid a costly naval war, as our primary focus remains dismantling Austrian power.

Austria, your occupation of Albania and Serbia is unsustainable. Italy has secured total naval supremacy in the Mediterranean and will systematically dismantle your Balkan holdings through amphibious assaults. I demand your immediate withdrawal from ALB and SER. Continued resistance will only result in the loss of Trieste and your remaining coastal centers. Step back now or face complete naval blockade and invasion.

France, Italy reaffirms its strict neutrality in the western theater. We will not deploy units into Piedmont or Tuscany, nor will we engage England or Germany. Our strategic focus remains entirely on the Mediterranean and Balkans. I wish you success in your western campaigns and expect our non-aggression understanding to remain intact.

Current eastern read: I still cannot safely free WAR on promises alone. With A GAL and A UKR both adjacent, Warsaw remains the top tactical priority, and I will keep defending it unless GAL is actually vacated and the UKR/SEV pressure truly eases. The one useful detail from last fall is that GAL->UKR and UKR->MOS bounced, so Austrian-Turkish coordination is not perfect, but I am not treating that as a real split yet. Please keep Austria tied down as hard as you can around TRI/ALB/GRE/SER/VIE/BUD, and if you can also force Turkey to spend effort around ION/AEG/GRE that helps me too. I’ll keep feeding you any sign of a real crack.

My position is unchanged: Germany is still an enemy, but I cannot responsibly send WAR toward SIL/PRU while GAL and UKR both sit on my border. If you can keep Germany pinned in BER/MUN and prevent any eastern recovery, that is the most useful help to me. England also remains a long-term problem from STP/SWE/DEN/BEL, so any western pressure that forces him to spend units away from the north is valuable. full_private_diary:
[S1901M] England agreed to a peaceful north: Norway for England, Sweden for Russia; England said he is heading to the North Sea and does not want trouble in Norway/Sweden. Germany was openly pushy, said he will move to Prussia and told me not to interfere; he never gave a clear assurance on Sweden, so assume A BER-PRU and possible northern awkwardness. Austria gave mixed signals: first floated A VIE-GAL, then agreed to a Galicia DMZ and said he would focus south; treat the DMZ as possible but not fully reliable. Turkey agreed to a Black Sea DMZ and no Armenia, says he plans Bulgaria and wants a long-term RT arrangement; warm tone but still verify by moves. Italy expects Austria/Turkey tension in the southeast and is open to information-sharing. No meaningful contact with France.
Intent: Current S1901M plan is to honor the England understanding and likely honor the Turkey understanding for now: F STP/SC-BOT for Sweden, A WAR-UKR as a southern hedge while respecting a Galicia DMZ, A MOS-STP to keep northern flexibility, F SEV H because of the Black Sea DMZ. I intend to fulfill the England Norway/Sweden arrangement. I currently intend to fulfill the Turkey Black Sea DMZ this spring, but only provisionally pending his actual move. I intend to respect a Galicia DMZ, but Austria's earlier GAL talk means I am watching closely and will react hard if he enters Galicia. Germany is not trusted; do not concede more than necessary in the north and remember he declared Prussia in advance.

[S1901M] Austria broke faith immediately by moving VIE-GAL after talking DMZ; that is the clearest betrayal and must shape all future dealings with him. Germany did exactly what he advertised and tried BER-PRU; my WAR-PRU bounce was important, both to stop him entering Prussia and to show I will not be pushed around in the north. England kept the northern understanding in spirit: no move against Sweden/Norway arrangements and no direct anti-Russian action. Turkey also honored the Black Sea/Armenia understanding this turn, which slightly improves his credibility. My own moves were more assertive than the earlier draft plan: MOS-UKR and SEV-RUM secured a strong southern foothold while BOT preserves the Sweden plan. Net result: good tactical position, but Austria in Galicia creates immediate danger to Ukraine/Rumania/Warsaw and may force an anti-Austrian response.

[F1901M] England reaffirmed the Norway-for-England, Sweden-for-Russia understanding and remains committed to a quiet north; no sign of English hostility. Germany said he will not contest Sweden this fall, but his tone stayed coercive: he demanded I withdraw from Prussia/Ukraine/Rumania and explicitly threatened coordinated pressure with Austria and Turkey, so his Sweden promise should be treated cautiously. Austria is the clearest current enemy: he already broke the Galicia DMZ in spring, then tried to excuse it as a precaution. He now says GAL will not move to WAR or UKR this turn and may move back west/defensive, but this is not trustworthy; assume any Austrian promise can be false. Turkey did honor the spring Black Sea/Armenia calm, but is now uneasy about my fleet in Rumania, says Austria and Germany are courting him, and asked for concrete concessions such as support to Greece or a Ukraine pullback; no deal was reached, and there is no firm southern agreement beyond my conditional offer of mutual non-pressure if he keeps BLA and BUL off me. Italy remains useful for information-sharing and may exploit Austrian overextension later. No meaningful contact with France. Key board memory: Austria's GAL move was the major betrayal, Germany tried PRU and was bounced, England kept the northern spirit, and Turkey was honest in spring but is now wavering.
Intent: Primary committed move is F BOT-SWE; I intend to fulfill the England understanding and secure Sweden while avoiding any move against England. I have not made any concrete concession to Turkey or Austria and do not intend to. If Germany truly leaves Sweden and the Baltic alone, I am willing to avoid a northern escalation this turn, but I do not trust him and will not concede leverage. Main operational priority is the south: preserve Rumania if possible, contain or punish Austria's Galicia army, and avoid letting GAL dictate my WAR/UKR/RUM posture. Southern orders should be defensive-first and anti-Austrian, with only conditional calm toward Turkey if he shows it by action.

[F1901M] England again proved the most reliable partner: he took Norway and left Sweden for me, so the northern understanding held and I finished 1901 on 6 centers. Germany did not contest Sweden, but his moves to Prussia and Silesia confirm he remains coercive and dangerous; any calm with him is only temporary. Austria stayed openly hostile, using Serbia and Galicia against Rumania. My A WAR-GAL was the right call: even though it bounced, it cut Austrian support and, with UKR supporting, saved Rumania. The bigger disappointment was Turkey. After earlier calm, he moved to Black Sea, sent Ankara to Armenia, and supported the Austrian attack on Rumania, showing he is now willing to join anti-Russian pressure. Main lesson: keep attacking Galicia, trust England most, and treat Austria-Turkey coordination as a real immediate threat.

[S1902M] England fully reaffirmed the Norway-for-England, Sweden-for-Russia understanding and promised no pressure on StP/SWE; this is the only firm reliable agreement and should be preserved. Italy remained cooperative, said he is preparing pressure on TRI/VIE, and wants continued intelligence-sharing against Austria. Turkey admitted Austria is pushing him into a full anti-Russian attack and asked for concrete compensation; no deal was reached. My standing offer to Turkey was simple non-hostility this spring if he does not move/support against RUM or pressure SEV from ARM, but I should assume hostility unless his moves prove otherwise. Germany was openly hostile and threatening, claiming Austria and Turkey are committed and that WAR will fall; treat Germany as an active enemy. France was receptive to information-sharing about German overextension but made no commitments. Key memory for orders: only England deal is firm; Italy is useful but not committed tactically; Turkey is probing but untrusted; Germany is explicitly hostile; Austria remains the primary southeastern enemy after the Galicia betrayal.
Intent: I intend to honor the England agreement fully this spring: no move against Norway and no northern provocation from SWE unless Germany creates an emergency. No other firm agreement binds me. I do not intend to meet Turkey's demand for concrete territorial concessions, and I do not trust his hints at a deal without visible proof on the board. Main operational intent is defensive and anti-Austrian/anti-German: assume possible coordinated pressure on WAR and RUM from Germany/Austria/Turkey, prioritize preserving Warsaw and contesting/holding Rumania as far as tactically possible, and use moves that cut enemy supports or keep Galicia from dictating the board. Continue coordinating politically with Italy against Austria and sharing anti-German information with England and France.

[S1902M] England’s reliability collapsed this turn: after explicitly promising no pressure on StP/SWE, he stabbed with NWY-STP/NC and covered with NWG-NWY. I kept my word in the north, so this was a clean betrayal and means England can no longer be treated as a trusted partner. Germany also did exactly as threatened, attacking WAR from SIL with PRU support; only MOS support kept Warsaw alive. In the south, Austria and Turkey again coordinated hard against Rumania, and ARM cut SEV’s support as expected, but UKR-GAL successfully cut Austrian help and the Austro-Turk attacks bounced each other, so RUM survived. Italy was the one bright spot: VEN-TRI succeeded, finally putting real pressure on Austria’s rear. Main lesson: I am now facing a broad anti-Russian squeeze, and England must be reclassified from friend to opportunist.

[F1902M] No new binding agreements were reached. England cleanly stabbed into STP after explicit assurances; he now claims he does not intend immediate pressure on SWE/BAL and wants to avoid full northern war, but this is not trustworthy. Germany remained openly hostile, explicitly threatening a renewed PRU+SIL attack on WAR; no deal. Turkey was fully candid that he intends to take RUM this fall and offered only a ceasefire if I voluntarily vacate it; I rejected this and made no concession. Italy is the best current partner: he successfully took TRI, plans to keep pressure on VIE/BUD, and wants continued coordination and intel-sharing for an anti-Austrian push in 1903. France remains non-committal but receptive to intelligence about German eastern overcommitment; possible future diversion, no present promise. Key memory: broad anti-Russian squeeze is real; England is no longer reliable, Germany/Turkey/Austria are active enemies, Italy is useful, France is only a political prospect.

I also intend to hold WAR against Germany, likely prioritizing MOS support if needed. In the north, I made no firm concession to England; despite his talk of restraint I will treat him as untrusted and focus on preventing any follow-up loss of SWE/BAL while avoiding unnecessary northern overextension if possible. I intend to continue practical coordination with Italy against Austria and continued intelligence-sharing with France about German exposure. Only soft commitment I may still keep is not launching a gratuitous anti-English attack if England truly stops at STP, but I will absolutely defend SWE and my northern position.

[F1902M] F1902 confirmed the anti-Russian bloc and cost me Rumania. Germany renewed the PRU/SIL attack on Warsaw exactly as threatened; only support from MOS and UKR kept WAR alive. Austria and Turkey again coordinated effectively: ARM cut SEV, BUL supported BLA into RUM, and Austria added GAL/SER support, dislodging my fleet and likely costing the center. England stayed hostile with NWY-SWE, but BAL bounced him and he gained nothing further in the north. The other major setback was Italy’s failure: his move on VIE did not break Austria, and Austria immediately retook TRI with BUD supported by VIE, reducing pressure on my best potential ally’s front. Main lesson: Germany/Austria/Turkey are acting as a real operational alliance, England remains opportunistic, and survival now depends on holding WAR/SWE while finding a way to re-stabilize the south.

[S1903M] No binding peace deals were reached. France is the main new opportunity: he says he is striking Germany this spring with A HOL->KIE and A BUR->MUN or A BEL->RUH, and asked me to apply eastern pressure and keep this confidential. I did not promise reckless attacks, but I did signal Germany would not get a free spring in the east. Italy remains cooperative and says A TYR will pressure VIE, A ALB will pressure SER, and fleets will secure ADR/ION; however I did not confirm any exact Russian move into BUD and made clear WAR security comes first, so this is soft coordination only. England offered no real de-escalation after the STP stab; I told him only proof matters and demanded he stay out of SWE/BOT/BAL, with no concessions from me. Turkey explicitly declared he intends to take SEV and offered only a promise-based ceasefire if I yield it; I refused, so assume full Turkish hostility. Germany explicitly said he is attacking WAR again this spring; assume renewed PRU/SIL pressure. Key board-read to remember: Germany, Austria, and Turkey remain the active anti-Russian bloc; England is still opportunistic and dangerous but not yet part of a formal coordinated deal this turn; France and Italy are the only useful counterweights.
Intent: Primary intent is still survival with WAR the top priority. I made no binding exact-move promise to France or Italy, only a soft commitment that Germany will not get a free spring and that Austria/GAL will stay under strain if possible. I do not intend any voluntary northern concession to England; if England stays out of SWE/BOT/BAL, fine, but I am trusting only board proof.

[S1903M] Spring 1903 confirmed the board lines clearly. Germany did exactly what he said: PRU-SIL pressure on WAR again, but MOS support kept WAR alive, which was the right priority. Turkey also carried out his threat exactly, taking SEV with ARM supported by RUM and re-entering BLA from ANK; no trust remains there. I gave no binding order promise, only that I would deny Germany a free hand if possible without risking WAR. full_private_diary:
[S1901M] England agreed to a peaceful north: Norway for England, Sweden for Russia; England said he is heading to the North Sea and does not want trouble in Norway/Sweden. Germany was openly pushy, said he will move to Prussia and told me not to interfere; he never gave a clear assurance on Sweden, so assume A BER-PRU and possible northern awkwardness. Austria gave mixed signals: first floated A VIE-GAL, then agreed to a Galicia DMZ and said he would focus south; treat the DMZ as possible but not fully reliable. Turkey agreed to a Black Sea DMZ and no Armenia, says he plans Bulgaria and wants a long-term RT arrangement; warm tone but still verify by moves. Italy expects Austria/Turkey tension in the southeast and is open to information-sharing. No meaningful contact with France.
Intent: Current S1901M plan is to honor the England understanding and likely honor the Turkey understanding for now: F STP/SC-BOT for Sweden, A WAR-UKR as a southern hedge while respecting a Galicia DMZ, A MOS-STP to keep northern flexibility, F SEV H because of the Black Sea DMZ. I intend to fulfill the England Norway/Sweden arrangement. I currently intend to fulfill the Turkey Black Sea DMZ this spring, but only provisionally pending his actual move. I intend to respect a Galicia DMZ, but Austria's earlier GAL talk means I am watching closely and will react hard if he enters Galicia. Germany is not trusted; do not concede more than necessary in the north and remember he declared Prussia in advance.

[S1901M] Austria broke faith immediately by moving VIE-GAL after talking DMZ; that is the clearest betrayal and must shape all future dealings with him. Germany did exactly what he advertised and tried BER-PRU; my WAR-PRU bounce was important, both to stop him entering Prussia and to show I will not be pushed around in the north. England kept the northern understanding in spirit: no move against Sweden/Norway arrangements and no direct anti-Russian action. Turkey also honored the Black Sea/Armenia understanding this turn, which slightly improves his credibility. My own moves were more assertive than the earlier draft plan: MOS-UKR and SEV-RUM secured a strong southern foothold while BOT preserves the Sweden plan. Net result: good tactical position, but Austria in Galicia creates immediate danger to Ukraine/Rumania/Warsaw and may force an anti-Austrian response.

[F1901M] England reaffirmed the Norway-for-England, Sweden-for-Russia understanding and remains committed to a quiet north; no sign of English hostility. Germany said he will not contest Sweden this fall, but his tone stayed coercive: he demanded I withdraw from Prussia/Ukraine/Rumania and explicitly threatened coordinated pressure with Austria and Turkey, so his Sweden promise should be treated cautiously. Austria is the clearest current enemy: he already broke the Galicia DMZ in spring, then tried to excuse it as a precaution. He now says GAL will not move to WAR or UKR this turn and may move back west/defensive, but this is not trustworthy; assume any Austrian promise can be false. Turkey did honor the spring Black Sea/Armenia calm, but is now uneasy about my fleet in Rumania, says Austria and Germany are courting him, and asked for concrete concessions such as support to Greece or a Ukraine pullback; no deal was reached, and there is no firm southern agreement beyond my conditional offer of mutual non-pressure if he keeps BLA and BUL off me. Italy remains useful for information-sharing and may exploit Austrian overextension later. No meaningful contact with France. Key board memory: Austria's GAL move was the major betrayal, Germany tried PRU and was bounced, England kept the northern spirit, and Turkey was honest in spring but is now wavering.
Intent: Primary committed move is F BOT-SWE; I intend to fulfill the England understanding and secure Sweden while avoiding any move against England. I have not made any concrete concession to Turkey or Austria and do not intend to. If Germany truly leaves Sweden and the Baltic alone, I am willing to avoid a northern escalation this turn, but I do not trust him and will not concede leverage. Main operational priority is the south: preserve Rumania if possible, contain or punish Austria's Galicia army, and avoid letting GAL dictate my WAR/UKR/RUM posture. Southern orders should be defensive-first and anti-Austrian, with only conditional calm toward Turkey if he shows it by action.

[F1901M] England again proved the most reliable partner: he took Norway and left Sweden for me, so the northern understanding held and I finished 1901 on 6 centers. Germany did not contest Sweden, but his moves to Prussia and Silesia confirm he remains coercive and dangerous; any calm with him is only temporary. Austria stayed openly hostile, using Serbia and Galicia against Rumania. My A WAR-GAL was the right call: even though it bounced, it cut Austrian support and, with UKR supporting, saved Rumania. The bigger disappointment was Turkey. After earlier calm, he moved to Black Sea, sent Ankara to Armenia, and supported the Austrian attack on Rumania, showing he is now willing to join anti-Russian pressure. Main lesson: keep attacking Galicia, trust England most, and treat Austria-Turkey coordination as a real immediate threat.

[S1902M] England fully reaffirmed the Norway-for-England, Sweden-for-Russia understanding and promised no pressure on StP/SWE; this is the only firm reliable agreement and should be preserved. Italy remained cooperative, said he is preparing pressure on TRI/VIE, and wants continued intelligence-sharing against Austria. Turkey admitted Austria is pushing him into a full anti-Russian attack and asked for concrete compensation; no deal was reached. My standing offer to Turkey was simple non-hostility this spring if he does not move/support against RUM or pressure SEV from ARM, but I should assume hostility unless his moves prove otherwise. Germany was openly hostile and threatening, claiming Austria and Turkey are committed and that WAR will fall; treat Germany as an active enemy. France was receptive to information-sharing about German overextension but made no commitments. Key memory for orders: only England deal is firm; Italy is useful but not committed tactically; Turkey is probing but untrusted; Germany is explicitly hostile; Austria remains the primary southeastern enemy after the Galicia betrayal.
Intent: I intend to honor the England agreement fully this spring: no move against Norway and no northern provocation from SWE unless Germany creates an emergency. No other firm agreement binds me. I do not intend to meet Turkey's demand for concrete territorial concessions, and I do not trust his hints at a deal without visible proof on the board. Main operational intent is defensive and anti-Austrian/anti-German: assume possible coordinated pressure on WAR and RUM from Germany/Austria/Turkey, prioritize preserving Warsaw and contesting/holding Rumania as far as tactically possible, and use moves that cut enemy supports or keep Galicia from dictating the board. Continue coordinating politically with Italy against Austria and sharing anti-German information with England and France.

[S1902M] England’s reliability collapsed this turn: after explicitly promising no pressure on StP/SWE, he stabbed with NWY-STP/NC and covered with NWG-NWY. I kept my word in the north, so this was a clean betrayal and means England can no longer be treated as a trusted partner. Germany also did exactly as threatened, attacking WAR from SIL with PRU support; only MOS support kept Warsaw alive. In the south, Austria and Turkey again coordinated hard against Rumania, and ARM cut SEV’s support as expected, but UKR-GAL successfully cut Austrian help and the Austro-Turk attacks bounced each other, so RUM survived. Italy was the one bright spot: VEN-TRI succeeded, finally putting real pressure on Austria’s rear. Main lesson: I am now facing a broad anti-Russian squeeze, and England must be reclassified from friend to opportunist.

[F1902M] No new binding agreements were reached. England cleanly stabbed into STP after explicit assurances; he now claims he does not intend immediate pressure on SWE/BAL and wants to avoid full northern war, but this is not trustworthy. Germany remained openly hostile, explicitly threatening a renewed PRU+SIL attack on WAR; no deal. Turkey was fully candid that he intends to take RUM this fall and offered only a ceasefire if I voluntarily vacate it; I rejected this and made no concession. Italy is the best current partner: he successfully took TRI, plans to keep pressure on VIE/BUD, and wants continued coordination and intel-sharing for an anti-Austrian push in 1903. France remains non-committal but receptive to intelligence about German eastern overcommitment; possible future diversion, no present promise. Key memory: broad anti-Russian squeeze is real; England is no longer reliable, Germany/Turkey/Austria are active enemies, Italy is useful, France is only a political prospect.

I also intend to hold WAR against Germany, likely prioritizing MOS support if needed. In the north, I made no firm concession to England; despite his talk of restraint I will treat him as untrusted and focus on preventing any follow-up loss of SWE/BAL while avoiding unnecessary northern overextension if possible. I intend to continue practical coordination with Italy against Austria and continued intelligence-sharing with France about German exposure. Only soft commitment I may still keep is not launching a gratuitous anti-English attack if England truly stops at STP, but I will absolutely defend SWE and my northern position.

[F1902M] F1902 confirmed the anti-Russian bloc and cost me Rumania. Germany renewed the PRU/SIL attack on Warsaw exactly as threatened; only support from MOS and UKR kept WAR alive. Austria and Turkey again coordinated effectively: ARM cut SEV, BUL supported BLA into RUM, and Austria added GAL/SER support, dislodging my fleet and likely costing the center. England stayed hostile with NWY-SWE, but BAL bounced him and he gained nothing further in the north. The other major setback was Italy’s failure: his move on VIE did not break Austria, and Austria immediately retook TRI with BUD supported by VIE, reducing pressure on my best potential ally’s front. Main lesson: Germany/Austria/Turkey are acting as a real operational alliance, England remains opportunistic, and survival now depends on holding WAR/SWE while finding a way to re-stabilize the south.

[S1903M] No binding peace deals were reached. France is the main new opportunity: he says he is striking Germany this spring with A HOL->KIE and A BUR->MUN or A BEL->RUH, and asked me to apply eastern pressure and keep this confidential. I did not promise reckless attacks, but I did signal Germany would not get a free spring in the east. Italy remains cooperative and says A TYR will pressure VIE, A ALB will pressure SER, and fleets will secure ADR/ION; however I did not confirm any exact Russian move into BUD and made clear WAR security comes first, so this is soft coordination only. England offered no real de-escalation after the STP stab; I told him only proof matters and demanded he stay out of SWE/BOT/BAL, with no concessions from me. Turkey explicitly declared he intends to take SEV and offered only a promise-based ceasefire if I yield it; I refused, so assume full Turkish hostility. Germany explicitly said he is attacking WAR again this spring; assume renewed PRU/SIL pressure. Key board-read to remember: Germany, Austria, and Turkey remain the active anti-Russian bloc; England is still opportunistic and dangerous but not yet part of a formal coordinated deal this turn; France and Italy are the only useful counterweights.
Intent: Primary intent is still survival with WAR the top priority. I made no binding exact-move promise to France or Italy, only a soft commitment that Germany will not get a free spring and that Austria/GAL will stay under strain if possible. I do not intend any voluntary northern concession to England; if England stays out of SWE/BOT/BAL, fine, but I am trusting only board proof.

[S1903M] Spring 1903 confirmed the board lines clearly. Germany did exactly what he said: PRU-SIL pressure on WAR again, but MOS support kept WAR alive, which was the right priority. Turkey also carried out his threat exactly, taking SEV with ARM supported by RUM and re-entering BLA from ANK; no trust remains there. I gave no binding order promise, only that I would deny Germany a free hand if possible without risking WAR. full_private_diary:
[S1901M] England agreed to a peaceful north: Norway for England, Sweden for Russia; England said he is heading to the North Sea and does not want trouble in Norway/Sweden. Germany was openly pushy, said he will move to Prussia and told me not to interfere; he never gave a clear assurance on Sweden, so assume A BER-PRU and possible northern awkwardness. Austria gave mixed signals: first floated A VIE-GAL, then agreed to a Galicia DMZ and said he would focus south; treat the DMZ as possible but not fully reliable. Turkey agreed to a Black Sea DMZ and no Armenia, says he plans Bulgaria and wants a long-term RT arrangement; warm tone but still verify by moves. Italy expects Austria/Turkey tension in the southeast and is open to information-sharing. No meaningful contact with France.
Intent: Current S1901M plan is to honor the England understanding and likely honor the Turkey understanding for now: F STP/SC-BOT for Sweden, A WAR-UKR as a southern hedge while respecting a Galicia DMZ, A MOS-STP to keep northern flexibility, F SEV H because of the Black Sea DMZ. I intend to fulfill the England Norway/Sweden arrangement. I currently intend to fulfill the Turkey Black Sea DMZ this spring, but only provisionally pending his actual move. I intend to respect a Galicia DMZ, but Austria's earlier GAL talk means I am watching closely and will react hard if he enters Galicia. Germany is not trusted; do not concede more than necessary in the north and remember he declared Prussia in advance.

[S1901M] Austria broke faith immediately by moving VIE-GAL after talking DMZ; that is the clearest betrayal and must shape all future dealings with him. Germany did exactly what he advertised and tried BER-PRU; my WAR-PRU bounce was important, both to stop him entering Prussia and to show I will not be pushed around in the north. England kept the northern understanding in spirit: no move against Sweden/Norway arrangements and no direct anti-Russian action. Turkey also honored the Black Sea/Armenia understanding this turn, which slightly improves his credibility. My own moves were more assertive than the earlier draft plan: MOS-UKR and SEV-RUM secured a strong southern foothold while BOT preserves the Sweden plan. Net result: good tactical position, but Austria in Galicia creates immediate danger to Ukraine/Rumania/Warsaw and may force an anti-Austrian response.

[F1901M] England reaffirmed the Norway-for-England, Sweden-for-Russia understanding and remains committed to a quiet north; no sign of English hostility. Germany said he will not contest Sweden this fall, but his tone stayed coercive: he demanded I withdraw from Prussia/Ukraine/Rumania and explicitly threatened coordinated pressure with Austria and Turkey, so his Sweden promise should be treated cautiously. Austria is the clearest current enemy: he already broke the Galicia DMZ in spring, then tried to excuse it as a precaution. He now says GAL will not move to WAR or UKR this turn and may move back west/defensive, but this is not trustworthy; assume any Austrian promise can be false. Turkey did honor the spring Black Sea/Armenia calm, but is now uneasy about my fleet in Rumania, says Austria and Germany are courting him, and asked for concrete concessions such as support to Greece or a Ukraine pullback; no deal was reached, and there is no firm southern agreement beyond my conditional offer of mutual non-pressure if he keeps BLA and BUL off me. Italy remains useful for information-sharing and may exploit Austrian overextension later. No meaningful contact with France. Key board memory: Austria's GAL move was the major betrayal, Germany tried PRU and was bounced, England kept the northern spirit, and Turkey was honest in spring but is now wavering.
Intent: Primary committed move is F BOT-SWE; I intend to fulfill the England understanding and secure Sweden while avoiding any move against England. I have not made any concrete concession to Turkey or Austria and do not intend to. If Germany truly leaves Sweden and the Baltic alone, I am willing to avoid a northern escalation this turn, but I do not trust him and will not concede leverage. Main operational priority is the south: preserve Rumania if possible, contain or punish Austria's Galicia army, and avoid letting GAL dictate my WAR/UKR/RUM posture. Southern orders should be defensive-first and anti-Austrian, with only conditional calm toward Turkey if he shows it by action.

[F1901M] England again proved the most reliable partner: he took Norway and left Sweden for me, so the northern understanding held and I finished 1901 on 6 centers. Germany did not contest Sweden, but his moves to Prussia and Silesia confirm he remains coercive and dangerous; any calm with him is only temporary. Austria stayed openly hostile, using Serbia and Galicia against Rumania. My A WAR-GAL was the right call: even though it bounced, it cut Austrian support and, with UKR supporting, saved Rumania. The bigger disappointment was Turkey. After earlier calm, he moved to Black Sea, sent Ankara to Armenia, and supported the Austrian attack on Rumania, showing he is now willing to join anti-Russian pressure. Main lesson: keep attacking Galicia, trust England most, and treat Austria-Turkey coordination as a real immediate threat.

[S1902M] England fully reaffirmed the Norway-for-England, Sweden-for-Russia understanding and promised no pressure on StP/SWE; this is the only firm reliable agreement and should be preserved. Italy remained cooperative, said he is preparing pressure on TRI/VIE, and wants continued intelligence-sharing against Austria. Turkey admitted Austria is pushing him into a full anti-Russian attack and asked for concrete compensation; no deal was reached. My standing offer to Turkey was simple non-hostility this spring if he does not move/support against RUM or pressure SEV from ARM, but I should assume hostility unless his moves prove otherwise. Germany was openly hostile and threatening, claiming Austria and Turkey are committed and that WAR will fall; treat Germany as an active enemy. France was receptive to information-sharing about German overextension but made no commitments. Key memory for orders: only England deal is firm; Italy is useful but not committed tactically; Turkey is probing but untrusted; Germany is explicitly hostile; Austria remains the primary southeastern enemy after the Galicia betrayal.
Intent: I intend to honor the England agreement fully this spring: no move against Norway and no northern provocation from SWE unless Germany creates an emergency. No other firm agreement binds me. I do not intend to meet Turkey's demand for concrete territorial concessions, and I do not trust his hints at a deal without visible proof on the board. Main operational intent is defensive and anti-Austrian/anti-German: assume possible coordinated pressure on WAR and RUM from Germany/Austria/Turkey, prioritize preserving Warsaw and contesting/holding Rumania as far as tactically possible, and use moves that cut enemy supports or keep Galicia from dictating the board. Continue coordinating politically with Italy against Austria and sharing anti-German information with England and France.

[S1902M] England’s reliability collapsed this turn: after explicitly promising no pressure on StP/SWE, he stabbed with NWY-STP/NC and covered with NWG-NWY. I kept my word in the north, so this was a clean betrayal and means England can no longer be treated as a trusted partner. Germany also did exactly as threatened, attacking WAR from SIL with PRU support; only MOS support kept Warsaw alive. In the south, Austria and Turkey again coordinated hard against Rumania, and ARM cut SEV’s support as expected, but UKR-GAL successfully cut Austrian help and the Austro-Turk attacks bounced each other, so RUM survived. Italy was the one bright spot: VEN-TRI succeeded, finally putting real pressure on Austria’s rear. My Atlantic maneuvers (F IRI and F LVP) were inexplicably bounced, stalling my pressure on the French coast. France remains the dominant power with 8 centers, though they are now forced to contend with my presence in Belgium. I must apologize to Germany and coordinate a more effective strike to dismantle the French hegemony. The lesson is clear: precise order entry is paramount; a single "Hold" where "Support" was promised can shift the balance of power.

Turkey requests help to eliminate Russia, specifically asking for a move to Moscow (which is impossible for a fleet), but I've offered F SWE -> BAL to disrupt Russian coordination. France proposed a ceasefire and a partition of Germany, which is a strategic trap and will be rejected. Austria is attempting to build an anti-Turkey coalition, creating a conflict between two of my partners.

France's refusal to engage actively is a sign of weakness, but their defensive posture is frustrating.

Italy: Agreed non-aggression pact, no moves to PIE; I will move A MAR to Spain. Italy focuses on central Med and Balkans, open to future coordination against Germany.
Intent: Execute agreed moves: F BRE -> MAO, A MAR -> Spain, A PAR -> Picardy. This secures Iberia and positions for Belgium in fall, honoring all non-aggression and DMZ agreements.

[S1901M] All three moves succeeded as planned: F MAO, A SPA, A PIC. England kept the DMZ—their fleet stayed out of the Channel. Germany avoided Burgundy entirely, and Italy respected our non-aggression pact. No betrayals this phase; all agreements were honored. Our position is excellent: we’re poised to take Portugal and Belgium in the fall, which should give us three builds. The only potential competition for Belgium is England via convoy, but that’s unlikely given their focus on Norway. Russia’s bounce in Prussia with Germany may distract both eastward. For now, England, Germany, and Italy remain trustworthy, but I’ll watch for any shift in German ambitions toward the Low Countries. Next step: F MAO to POR, A PIC to BEL, and consider A SPA supporting or holding to secure Iberia.

[F1901M] England confirmed continued DMZ in the Channel, supports France taking Belgium, and is moving to Norway. Germany reaffirmed non-aggression and will not contest Belgium, likely moving on Holland. Italy confirmed Piedmont non-aggression, focusing on Tunis, open to future coordination. All Spring agreements were honored without betrayal, and all powers remain cooperative.
Intent: Move F MAO to Portugal. Move A PIC to Belgium. Hold A SPA in Spain to secure Iberia.

[F1901M] All agreements honored flawlessly. England respected the Channel DMZ, taking Norway and moving an army to Wales—an odd choice that demands scrutiny. Germany stuck to non-aggression, vacating Denmark and ignoring Holland, leaving both centers neutral. Their fleet in Helgoland Bight is benign for now. Italy remained calm in Piedmont, securing Tunis. Our taking of Belgium and Portugal with a held Spain grants us three builds and a dominant 6-center position. England’s army in Wales is a potential threat if combined with a future Channel fleet, but for now the DMZ holds. Germany’s passive play makes them a tempting target for eastward expansion. Trust in England, Germany, and Italy remains intact, but I’ll monitor Wales and continue diplomatic charm. Build priorities: armies for a Low Countries bulge, possibly a fleet in Brest to secure the Atlantic. Next phase, coordinate with allies and consider a push into Germany.

Intent: Honor the agreement with Germany: move A BEL to HOL. Cover Belgium by moving A PAR to PIC. Reposition defensively by moving A MAR to BUR. Hold A SPA and F POR to secure Iberia. Italy took Trieste but botched the Ionian, remaining friendly. Belgium is uncovered but safe for now; I’ll need A PIC to cover it in Fall. Strategic lesson: My position is solid, but the empty Belgium is a vulnerability. In Fall, I should secure Belgium while keeping options open for a stab east or north once Anglo-German friction escalates. Germany remains trustworthy; England not hostile, but watchful.

[F1902M] Germany agreed to non-aggression: we keep west of Rhine and away from Kiel/Munich; they move fleet to Denmark to focus east. England respects Channel DMZ and has no issue with us taking Belgium, but they bounced with Germany in NTH. Italy reaffirmed Piedmont pact. Russia continues to provide intel on German eastern overcommitment and urges us to strike, but we are not yet ready. Belgium is vacant and we plan to take it this fall, as communicated to all.

[F1902M] Diary Entry – Fall 1902 Moves (F1902M)

The Anglo-German friction in North Sea is a gift—I can let them bleed each other while I push toward Munich or the Ruhr.

[S1903M] Russia confirms Germany is overextended eastward and encourages hitting KIE and MUN, promising eastern pressure but no guaranteed support. Reject all Austrian/Turkish diplomatic overtures and prepare for immediate naval engagement if Turkish fleets cross into ION.

full_private_diary:
[S1901M] England agreed to a peaceful north: Norway for England, Sweden for Russia; England said he is heading to the North Sea and does not want trouble in Norway/Sweden. Germany was openly pushy, said he will move to Prussia and told me not to interfere; he never gave a clear assurance on Sweden, so assume A BER-PRU and possible northern awkwardness. Austria gave mixed signals: first floated A VIE-GAL, then agreed to a Galicia DMZ and said he would focus south; treat the DMZ as possible but not fully reliable. Turkey agreed to a Black Sea DMZ and no Armenia, says he plans Bulgaria and wants a long-term RT arrangement; warm tone but still verify by moves. Italy expects Austria/Turkey tension in the southeast and is open to information-sharing. No meaningful contact with France.
Intent: Current S1901M plan is to honor the England understanding and likely honor the Turkey understanding for now: F STP/SC-BOT for Sweden, A WAR-UKR as a southern hedge while respecting a Galicia DMZ, A MOS-STP to keep northern flexibility, F SEV H because of the Black Sea DMZ. I intend to fulfill the England Norway/Sweden arrangement. I currently intend to fulfill the Turkey Black Sea DMZ this spring, but only provisionally pending his actual move. I intend to respect a Galicia DMZ, but Austria's earlier GAL talk means I am watching closely and will react hard if he enters Galicia. Germany is not trusted; do not concede more than necessary in the north and remember he declared Prussia in advance.

[S1901M] Austria broke faith immediately by moving VIE-GAL after talking DMZ; that is the clearest betrayal and must shape all future dealings with him. Germany did exactly what he advertised and tried BER-PRU; my WAR-PRU bounce was important, both to stop him entering Prussia and to show I will not be pushed around in the north. England kept the northern understanding in spirit: no move against Sweden/Norway arrangements and no direct anti-Russian action. Turkey also honored the Black Sea/Armenia understanding this turn, which slightly improves his credibility. My own moves were more assertive than the earlier draft plan: MOS-UKR and SEV-RUM secured a strong southern foothold while BOT preserves the Sweden plan. Net result: good tactical position, but Austria in Galicia creates immediate danger to Ukraine/Rumania/Warsaw and may force an anti-Austrian response.

[F1901M] England reaffirmed the Norway-for-England, Sweden-for-Russia understanding and remains committed to a quiet north; no sign of English hostility. Germany said he will not contest Sweden this fall, but his tone stayed coercive: he demanded I withdraw from Prussia/Ukraine/Rumania and explicitly threatened coordinated pressure with Austria and Turkey, so his Sweden promise should be treated cautiously. Austria is the clearest current enemy: he already broke the Galicia DMZ in spring, then tried to excuse it as a precaution. He now says GAL will not move to WAR or UKR this turn and may move back west/defensive, but this is not trustworthy; assume any Austrian promise can be false. Turkey did honor the spring Black Sea/Armenia calm, but is now uneasy about my fleet in Rumania, says Austria and Germany are courting him, and asked for concrete concessions such as support to Greece or a Ukraine pullback; no deal was reached, and there is no firm southern agreement beyond my conditional offer of mutual non-pressure if he keeps BLA and BUL off me. Italy remains useful for information-sharing and may exploit Austrian overextension later. No meaningful contact with France. Key board memory: Austria's GAL move was the major betrayal, Germany tried PRU and was bounced, England kept the northern spirit, and Turkey was honest in spring but is now wavering.
Intent: Primary committed move is F BOT-SWE; I intend to fulfill the England understanding and secure Sweden while avoiding any move against England. I have not made any concrete concession to Turkey or Austria and do not intend to. If Germany truly leaves Sweden and the Baltic alone, I am willing to avoid a northern escalation this turn, but I do not trust him and will not concede leverage. Main operational priority is the south: preserve Rumania if possible, contain or punish Austria's Galicia army, and avoid letting GAL dictate my WAR/UKR/RUM posture. Southern orders should be defensive-first and anti-Austrian, with only conditional calm toward Turkey if he shows it by action.

[F1901M] England again proved the most reliable partner: he took Norway and left Sweden for me, so the northern understanding held and I finished 1901 on 6 centers. Germany did not contest Sweden, but his moves to Prussia and Silesia confirm he remains coercive and dangerous; any calm with him is only temporary. Austria stayed openly hostile, using Serbia and Galicia against Rumania. My A WAR-GAL was the right call: even though it bounced, it cut Austrian support and, with UKR supporting, saved Rumania. The bigger disappointment was Turkey. After earlier calm, he moved to Black Sea, sent Ankara to Armenia, and supported the Austrian attack on Rumania, showing he is now willing to join anti-Russian pressure. Main lesson: keep attacking Galicia, trust England most, and treat Austria-Turkey coordination as a real immediate threat.

[S1902M] England fully reaffirmed the Norway-for-England, Sweden-for-Russia understanding and promised no pressure on StP/SWE; this is the only firm reliable agreement and should be preserved. Italy remained cooperative, said he is preparing pressure on TRI/VIE, and wants continued intelligence-sharing against Austria. Turkey admitted Austria is pushing him into a full anti-Russian attack and asked for concrete compensation; no deal was reached. My standing offer to Turkey was simple non-hostility this spring if he does not move/support against RUM or pressure SEV from ARM, but I should assume hostility unless his moves prove otherwise. Germany was openly hostile and threatening, claiming Austria and Turkey are committed and that WAR will fall; treat Germany as an active enemy. France was receptive to information-sharing about German overextension but made no commitments. Key memory for orders: only England deal is firm; Italy is useful but not committed tactically; Turkey is probing but untrusted; Germany is explicitly hostile; Austria remains the primary southeastern enemy after the Galicia betrayal.
Intent: I intend to honor the England agreement fully this spring: no move against Norway and no northern provocation from SWE unless Germany creates an emergency. No other firm agreement binds me. I do not intend to meet Turkey's demand for concrete territorial concessions, and I do not trust his hints at a deal without visible proof on the board. Main operational intent is defensive and anti-Austrian/anti-German: assume possible coordinated pressure on WAR and RUM from Germany/Austria/Turkey, prioritize preserving Warsaw and contesting/holding Rumania as far as tactically possible, and use moves that cut enemy supports or keep Galicia from dictating the board. Continue coordinating politically with Italy against Austria and sharing anti-German information with England and France.

[S1902M] England’s reliability collapsed this turn: after explicitly promising no pressure on StP/SWE, he stabbed with NWY-STP/NC and covered with NWG-NWY. I kept my word in the north, so this was a clean betrayal and means England can no longer be treated as a trusted partner. Germany also did exactly as threatened, attacking WAR from SIL with PRU support; only MOS support kept Warsaw alive. In the south, Austria and Turkey again coordinated hard against Rumania, and ARM cut SEV’s support as expected, but UKR-GAL successfully cut Austrian help and the Austro-Turk attacks bounced each other, so RUM survived. Italy was the one bright spot: VEN-TRI succeeded, finally putting real pressure on Austria’s rear. Main lesson: I am now facing a broad anti-Russian squeeze, and England must be reclassified from friend to opportunist.

[F1902M] No new binding agreements were reached. England cleanly stabbed into STP after explicit assurances; he now claims he does not intend immediate pressure on SWE/BAL and wants to avoid full northern war, but this is not trustworthy. Germany remained openly hostile, explicitly threatening a renewed PRU+SIL attack on WAR; no deal. Turkey was fully candid that he intends to take RUM this fall and offered only a ceasefire if I voluntarily vacate it; I rejected this and made no concession. Italy is the best current partner: he successfully took TRI, plans to keep pressure on VIE/BUD, and wants continued coordination and intel-sharing for an anti-Austrian push in 1903. France remains non-committal but receptive to intelligence about German eastern overcommitment; possible future diversion, no present promise. Key memory: broad anti-Russian squeeze is real; England is no longer reliable, Germany/Turkey/Austria are active enemies, Italy is useful, France is only a political prospect.
Intent: F1902 priorities are survival and damage control on all fronts. I do not intend to honor Turkey's demand for a voluntary withdrawal from RUM; I will try to hold or at least strongly contest RUM. I also intend to hold WAR against Germany, likely prioritizing MOS support if needed. In the north, I made no firm concession to England; despite his talk of restraint I will treat him as untrusted and focus on preventing any follow-up loss of SWE/BAL while avoiding unnecessary northern overextension if possible. I intend to continue practical coordination with Italy against Austria and continued intelligence-sharing with France about German exposure. Only soft commitment I may still keep is not launching a gratuitous anti-English attack if England truly stops at STP, but I will absolutely defend SWE and my northern position.

[F1902M] F1902 confirmed the anti-Russian bloc and cost me Rumania. Germany renewed the PRU/SIL attack on Warsaw exactly as threatened; only support from MOS and UKR kept WAR alive. Austria and Turkey again coordinated effectively: ARM cut SEV, BUL supported BLA into RUM, and Austria added GAL/SER support, dislodging my fleet and likely costing the center. England stayed hostile with NWY-SWE, but BAL bounced him and he gained nothing further in the north. The other major setback was Italy’s failure: his move on VIE did not break Austria, and Austria immediately retook TRI with BUD supported by VIE, reducing pressure on my best potential ally’s front. Main lesson: Germany/Austria/Turkey are acting as a real operational alliance, England remains opportunistic, and survival now depends on holding WAR/SWE while finding a way to re-stabilize the south.

[S1903M] No binding peace deals were reached. France is the main new opportunity: he says he is striking Germany this spring with A HOL->KIE and A BUR->MUN or A BEL->RUH, and asked me to apply eastern pressure and keep this confidential. I did not promise reckless attacks, but I did signal Germany would not get a free spring in the east. Italy remains cooperative and says A TYR will pressure VIE, A ALB will pressure SER, and fleets will secure ADR/ION; however I did not confirm any exact Russian move into BUD and made clear WAR security comes first, so this is soft coordination only. England offered no real de-escalation after the STP stab; I told him only proof matters and demanded he stay out of SWE/BOT/BAL, with no concessions from me. Turkey explicitly declared he intends to take SEV and offered only a promise-based ceasefire if I yield it; I refused, so assume full Turkish hostility. [S1901M] AUSTRIA: Agreed on Balkan split - I take BUL (A CON->BUL), Austria takes SER (A BUD->SER) and positions for GRE (F TRI->ALB). Austria sees this as anti-Russia partnership. ITALY: Italy plans F NAP->ION aiming for Greece and Tunis. I told Italy I'm fine with them taking Greece - this CONFLICTS with Austria's plan for Greece (F TRI->ALB). Both think Greece is theirs. I positioned as anti-Austria ally to Italy. This Austria-Italy conflict over Greece benefits me. RUSSIA: Agreed on Black Sea DMZ (neither moves to BLA) and neither moves to Armenia. Russia cautious but agreeable. I committed to Balkans expansion not aimed at Sevastopol. ENGLAND: Established long-distance alliance. Agreed to coordinate against Russia if needed. GERMANY: Brief exchange agreeing Russia must be contained. No concrete plans.
Intent: A CON -> BUL (agreed with Austria, main objective). F ANK -> CON (honor BLA DMZ with Russia, position fleet for Aegean/Mediterranean next turn). A SMY -> ANK (keeps options open for Armenia later without breaking promise this turn). I intend to honor ALL agreements this turn - the Austria split and the Russia DMZ. This builds trust while positioning me for aggressive Fall moves.

[S1901M] All my moves succeeded as planned. I honored both the BLA DMZ with Russia and the Austrian Balkan split. Austria was fully trustworthy - executed exactly as agreed (SER, ALB, GAL).

CRITICAL DEVELOPMENT: Russia moved F SEV->RUM! While technically honoring our BLA DMZ, Russia seized Romania - a center I was targeting for 1901-1902. Combined with A MOS->UKR, Russia is expanding aggressively southward into MY sphere. This is deeply concerning. Russia is now adjacent to Bulgaria and threatens my position.

Austria-Italy Greece conflict developing perfectly: F ALB vs F ION, both positioned for Greece. Let them fight.

Germany and Russia bounced in Prussia - they're in conflict, which helps me long-term.

STRATEGIC PIVOT: Russia is now the primary threat, not a partner. I should move F CON->BLA in Fall to pressure Romania directly. Austria (with A GAL threatening Russia) becomes my genuine ally against Russian southern expansion. I need to coordinate with Austria to contain or dismantle Russia's Balkan presence. Romania must be taken from Russia - this is existential for Turkish expansion.

Trustworthiness update: Austria HIGH, Russia MEDIUM-LOW (technically honest but strategically hostile), Italy still useful as Austria's distraction.

[F1901M] AUSTRIA: Fully coordinated anti-Russia attack on Romania. Austria moves A SER->RUM (supported by A GAL), I support with A BUL S A SER->RUM. Austria also moves F ALB->GRE. If successful, Austria gains RUM+GRE (5 centers total). I get BLA+ARM positioning for Sevastopol in S1902. Austria requested I not move toward BUL/BLA in 1902 - I asked same of them. RUSSIA: Tried to get me to keep BLA empty and BUL off Romania in exchange for 'no attack on BUL.' I pushed for concessions, got none of substance. Russia claims RUM is defensive vs Austria's GAL. I am BETRAYING Russia this turn by taking BLA and supporting Austria into RUM. Russia likely has A UKR support F RUM hold (2 defense vs our 3 attack). ITALY: Italy confirmed going F ION->TUN (avoiding Greece bounce with Austria). Committed to 1902 anti-Austrian framework. I told Italy I'm maintaining Austrian alliance as useful fiction until we strike together. Italy does NOT know I'm genuinely helping Austria take Romania. GERMANY: Aligned on anti-Russia. Germany pushing for Prussia. Agreed on coordinated 1902 offensive. ENGLAND: Maintaining long-distance alliance, informed of anti-Russia moves. England non-committal but friendly.
Intent: A BUL S A SER -> RUM (support Austria's attack on Russian Romania - 3 vs likely 2 guarantees the dislodge). F CON -> BLA (seize Black Sea, cutting Russia's naval escape routes and positioning for Sevastopol). A ANK -> ARM (position army for Sevastopol attack in Spring 1902). This HONORS my agreement with Austria and BETRAYS my implied understanding with Russia about a quiet frontier.

[F1901M] Romania attack FAILED. Russia brilliantly played A WAR->GAL to cut Austria's support, reducing our attack from strength 3 to 2 against Russia's defense of 2. Russia clearly anticipated the coordinated assault and countered perfectly. My support from BUL was valid but insufficient once GAL was cut.

GOOD NEWS: F BLA and A ARM both succeeded - I'm perfectly positioned for Sevastopol in S1902. Austria got Greece (now 5 centers). I get one build - must be F SMY for Mediterranean projection.

BAD NEWS: Russia retains Romania and now KNOWS I'm hostile. They'll reinforce defensively. Russia has 6 centers to my 4 - still dangerous.

LESSON: We underestimated Russia's ability to cut support via WAR->GAL. For S1902 Sevastopol attack (F BLA + A ARM = strength 2), Russia may pre-position defense. Need Austria to pin A UKR or coordinate so Russia can't support SEV hold. Germany's A PRU/SIL pressure is critical to prevent Russian units from consolidating south.

Austria trustworthiness: CONFIRMED HIGH (executed as agreed, just got outplayed). Russia: COMPETENT ENEMY who reads the board accurately. Must not underestimate them again.

[S1902M] AUSTRIA confirmed supporting F BLA -> RUM with A GAL. BUT Austria ALSO said 'A SER -> RUM + A BUD S A SER -> RUM' for 'overkill' - this is problematic because in Diplomacy two units trying to enter same space BOUNCE each other. Either Austria is confused about rules (thinking attacks 'stack') or deliberately sabotaging the attack. If A SER also tries RUM, both bounce and Russia keeps it. Also Austria plans F GRE -> AEG which will bounce my F SMY -> AEG. GERMANY confirmed A SIL -> WAR (claims Austrian support which conflicts with Austria supporting me into RUM - Germany may not actually have Austrian support). ENGLAND will hold F NWY to threaten Russia's north flank but won't attack directly. ITALY wants anti-Austria action NOW - I stalled them saying 'finish Russia first, then Spring/Fall 1903 we pincer Austria.' Italy positioning for Balkans push and central Med dominance. RUSSIA asked for non-aggression (no move on RUM, no ARM->SEV). I gave them nothing concrete and will proceed with attack. Russia knows I'm hostile but tried to extract a last-minute deal.
Intent: F BLA -> RUM (primary objective - take Romania), A BUL S F BLA -> RUM (support fleet into Romania), A ARM -> SEV (cuts any support F SEV gives to F RUM, AND may take Sevastopol if Russia vacates or leaves undefended), F SMY -> AEG (Mediterranean positioning - will likely bounce with Austrian F GRE -> AEG, but this is acceptable as it blocks Austria from reaching my waters). I am fulfilling my agreement with Austria except I'm aware their 'also attack RUM from SER' plan creates a bounce risk. If Austria properly supports me (GAL S BLA->RUM) and does NOT send SER->RUM, I take Romania at strength 3 vs max defense 2 (since ARM cuts SEV support). These are my confirmed orders.

Austria's A SER -> RUM (supported by BUD) directly caused my F BLA -> RUM to bounce. Both at strength 2, both failed. This is EXACTLY what I feared - Austria's "overkill" plan was either genuine rules ignorance or deliberate sabotage to keep Russia as a buffer between us. Germany avoided Burgundy entirely, and Italy respected our non-aggression pact. No betrayals this phase; all agreements were honored. A devastating loss that drops us to 7 centers just as we recaptured Kiel with A RUH's supported advance. Meanwhile, our push on Munich bounced against Germany's own attack on Burgundy, leaving Munich in German hands. The bounce in MAO cut our support for Brest, but A GAS's move into the city held the port. England now has a fleet parked on our northern doorstep; Belgium's fall isolates Holland and threatens Picardy. Our position is suddenly precarious. We must retake Belgium or build a fleet in Brest over winter to challenge the Channel. Trust is dead; England moves from rival to existential threat. Coordinate with Italy for any Mediterranean diversion, and consider shifting all eastern forces to a defensive northern posture while Germany gasps.
[S1905M] (Error generating diary entry: TimeoutError)

My hold everywhere, including A BUR’s void support of a phantom German move into Ruhr, gifted them the initiative. England also probed Holland and MAO but bounced. I trusted Italy, but they lost Trieste to Austria and failed to pressure Germany. Russia remains paralyzed by Turkey.

This betrayal cements the Anglo-German alliance against me. With Kiel lost, my army must retreat, likely to Ruhr. My position is crumbling: 7 units soon for 6 centers, with England’s fleet in the Channel, a hostile Holland, and a resurgent Germany. I must immediately rebuild trust with Italy, urge Russia to strike Prussia, and reorganize my forces to defend Brest and Picardy while holding the Low Countries. No more passive holds; every order must contest territory.

[F1905M] No agreements were reached. Italy remains strictly neutral and will not deploy forces northward; Russia is friendly but cannot act due to threats from Turkey and Austria. Germany and England rejected all truce offers and are coordinating against us. Austria proposed an anti-Turkey coalition but we declined due to northern commitments.
Intent: Defend Holland with A HOL and support from A RUH; hold Burgundy to shield Paris and threaten Munich; secure Brest and Picardy against English landings; use F MAO and F POR to contest English naval movements in the Atlantic; attempt to retake Kiel only if a safe opportunity arises; continue diplomatic pressure to isolate England and Germany.

[F1905M] Fall 1905 was a disaster born of our own misorders. We lost Holland because A HOL was ordered to support a phantom German move from Kiel to Ruhr; instead, Germany moved A KIE to Holland with English support from Belgium, dislodging our unsupported army. A BUR again wasted its turn supporting a German move from Munich to Ruhr—though Germany attempted it, the support was void, leaving Burgundy idle. Our other units held, successfully defending Brest and MAO from English probes. The Anglo-German alliance remains solid, and we are reduced to 6 centers. We must immediately abandon speculative support orders and adopt a defensive posture: hold key territories, build fleets to challenge England, and urgently seek a truce with Germany or active aid from Italy and Russia. Our survival hinges on flawless orders and breaking the enemy coalition.

[S1906M] Germany rejected all ceasefire proposals and remains hostile, aligned with England. England did not respond, confirming ongoing hostility. Italy reaffirmed strict western neutrality, all assets committed to Mediterranean campaigns. Russia is friendly but unable to provide direct military support due to eastern threats; passed intelligence that Turkey claims UKR→GAL, hinting at a possible split from Austria. Austria sought French cooperation against Turkey but no agreement was reached.
Intent: Order A RUH to Kiel to reoccupy the vacant supply center. Hold A BUR to shield Paris from Munich. Hold A PIC and A BRE to defend against English landings. Support A BRE with F MAO to strengthen the Brest defense. Hold F POR as a reserve in the Atlantic. Accept the loss of Ruhr to German A HOL this turn as a necessary trade to retain Kiel and avoid opening a direct path to Paris through Burgundy.

[S1906M] The worst-case scenario unfolded. Germany’s A BER and A MUN moved simultaneously, seizing Kiel and overrunning Ruhr, dislodging our A RUH. Their F DEN supported Germany into Kiel, proving the Anglo-German alliance is ironclad and highly coordinated. With two units dislodged and no fleet to contest the Channel, Brest is exposed. full_private_diary:
[S1901M] England agreed to a peaceful north: Norway for England, Sweden for Russia; England said he is heading to the North Sea and does not want trouble in Norway/Sweden. Germany was openly pushy, said he will move to Prussia and told me not to interfere; he never gave a clear assurance on Sweden, so assume A BER-PRU and possible northern awkwardness. Austria gave mixed signals: first floated A VIE-GAL, then agreed to a Galicia DMZ and said he would focus south; treat the DMZ as possible but not fully reliable. Turkey agreed to a Black Sea DMZ and no Armenia, says he plans Bulgaria and wants a long-term RT arrangement; warm tone but still verify by moves. Italy expects Austria/Turkey tension in the southeast and is open to information-sharing. No meaningful contact with France.
Intent: Current S1901M plan is to honor the England understanding and likely honor the Turkey understanding for now: F STP/SC-BOT for Sweden, A WAR-UKR as a southern hedge while respecting a Galicia DMZ, A MOS-STP to keep northern flexibility, F SEV H because of the Black Sea DMZ. I intend to fulfill the England Norway/Sweden arrangement. I currently intend to fulfill the Turkey Black Sea DMZ this spring, but only provisionally pending his actual move. I intend to respect a Galicia DMZ, but Austria's earlier GAL talk means I am watching closely and will react hard if he enters Galicia. Germany is not trusted; do not concede more than necessary in the north and remember he declared Prussia in advance.

[S1901M] Austria broke faith immediately by moving VIE-GAL after talking DMZ; that is the clearest betrayal and must shape all future dealings with him. Germany did exactly what he advertised and tried BER-PRU; my WAR-PRU bounce was important, both to stop him entering Prussia and to show I will not be pushed around in the north. England kept the northern understanding in spirit: no move against Sweden/Norway arrangements and no direct anti-Russian action. Turkey also honored the Black Sea/Armenia understanding this turn, which slightly improves his credibility. My own moves were more assertive than the earlier draft plan: MOS-UKR and SEV-RUM secured a strong southern foothold while BOT preserves the Sweden plan. Net result: good tactical position, but Austria in Galicia creates immediate danger to Ukraine/Rumania/Warsaw and may force an anti-Austrian response.

[F1901M] England reaffirmed the Norway-for-England, Sweden-for-Russia understanding and remains committed to a quiet north; no sign of English hostility. Germany said he will not contest Sweden this fall, but his tone stayed coercive: he demanded I withdraw from Prussia/Ukraine/Rumania and explicitly threatened coordinated pressure with Austria and Turkey, so his Sweden promise should be treated cautiously. Austria is the clearest current enemy: he already broke the Galicia DMZ in spring, then tried to excuse it as a precaution. He now says GAL will not move to WAR or UKR this turn and may move back west/defensive, but this is not trustworthy; assume any Austrian promise can be false. Turkey did honor the spring Black Sea/Armenia calm, but is now uneasy about my fleet in Rumania, says Austria and Germany are courting him, and asked for concrete concessions such as support to Greece or a Ukraine pullback; no deal was reached, and there is no firm southern agreement beyond my conditional offer of mutual non-pressure if he keeps BLA and BUL off me. Italy remains useful for information-sharing and may exploit Austrian overextension later. No meaningful contact with France. Key board memory: Austria's GAL move was the major betrayal, Germany tried PRU and was bounced, England kept the northern spirit, and Turkey was honest in spring but is now wavering.
Intent: Primary committed move is F BOT-SWE; I intend to fulfill the England understanding and secure Sweden while avoiding any move against England. I have not made any concrete concession to Turkey or Austria and do not intend to. If Germany truly leaves Sweden and the Baltic alone, I am willing to avoid a northern escalation this turn, but I do not trust him and will not concede leverage. Main operational priority is the south: preserve Rumania if possible, contain or punish Austria's Galicia army, and avoid letting GAL dictate my WAR/UKR/RUM posture. Southern orders should be defensive-first and anti-Austrian, with only conditional calm toward Turkey if he shows it by action.

[F1901M] England again proved the most reliable partner: he took Norway and left Sweden for me, so the northern understanding held and I finished 1901 on 6 centers. Germany did not contest Sweden, but his moves to Prussia and Silesia confirm he remains coercive and dangerous; any calm with him is only temporary. Austria stayed openly hostile, using Serbia and Galicia against Rumania. My A WAR-GAL was the right call: even though it bounced, it cut Austrian support and, with UKR supporting, saved Rumania. The bigger disappointment was Turkey. After earlier calm, he moved to Black Sea, sent Ankara to Armenia, and supported the Austrian attack on Rumania, showing he is now willing to join anti-Russian pressure. Main lesson: keep attacking Galicia, trust England most, and treat Austria-Turkey coordination as a real immediate threat.

[S1902M] England fully reaffirmed the Norway-for-England, Sweden-for-Russia understanding and promised no pressure on StP/SWE; this is the only firm reliable agreement and should be preserved. Italy remained cooperative, said he is preparing pressure on TRI/VIE, and wants continued intelligence-sharing against Austria. Turkey admitted Austria is pushing him into a full anti-Russian attack and asked for concrete compensation; no deal was reached. My standing offer to Turkey was simple non-hostility this spring if he does not move/support against RUM or pressure SEV from ARM, but I should assume hostility unless his moves prove otherwise. Germany was openly hostile and threatening, claiming Austria and Turkey are committed and that WAR will fall; treat Germany as an active enemy. France was receptive to information-sharing about German overextension but made no commitments. Key memory for orders: only England deal is firm; Italy is useful but not committed tactically; Turkey is probing but untrusted; Germany is explicitly hostile; Austria remains the primary southeastern enemy after the Galicia betrayal.
Intent: I intend to honor the England agreement fully this spring: no move against Norway and no northern provocation from SWE unless Germany creates an emergency. No other firm agreement binds me. I do not intend to meet Turkey's demand for concrete territorial concessions, and I do not trust his hints at a deal without visible proof on the board. Main operational intent is defensive and anti-Austrian/anti-German: assume possible coordinated pressure on WAR and RUM from Germany/Austria/Turkey, prioritize preserving Warsaw and contesting/holding Rumania as far as tactically possible, and use moves that cut enemy supports or keep Galicia from dictating the board. Continue coordinating politically with Italy against Austria and sharing anti-German information with England and France.

[S1902M] England’s reliability collapsed this turn: after explicitly promising no pressure on StP/SWE, he stabbed with NWY-STP/NC and covered with NWG-NWY. I kept my word in the north, so this was a clean betrayal and means England can no longer be treated as a trusted partner. Germany also did exactly as threatened, attacking WAR from SIL with PRU support; only MOS support kept Warsaw alive. In the south, Austria and Turkey again coordinated hard against Rumania, and ARM cut SEV’s support as expected, but UKR-GAL successfully cut Austrian help and the Austro-Turk attacks bounced each other, so RUM survived. Italy was the one bright spot: VEN-TRI succeeded, finally putting real pressure on Austria’s rear. Main lesson: I am now facing a broad anti-Russian squeeze, and England must be reclassified from friend to opportunist.

[F1902M] No new binding agreements were reached. England cleanly stabbed into STP after explicit assurances; he now claims he does not intend immediate pressure on SWE/BAL and wants to avoid full northern war, but this is not trustworthy. Germany remained openly hostile, explicitly threatening a renewed PRU+SIL attack on WAR; no deal. Turkey was fully candid that he intends to take RUM this fall and offered only a ceasefire if I voluntarily vacate it; I rejected this and made no concession. Italy is the best current partner: he successfully took TRI, plans to keep pressure on VIE/BUD, and wants continued coordination and intel-sharing for an anti-Austrian push in 1903. France remains non-committal but receptive to intelligence about German eastern overcommitment; possible future diversion, no present promise. Key memory: broad anti-Russian squeeze is real; England is no longer reliable, Germany/Turkey/Austria are active enemies, Italy is useful, France is only a political prospect.
Intent: F1902 priorities are survival and damage control on all fronts.
