full_private_diary:
[S1901M] England agreed to a peaceful north: Norway for England, Sweden for Russia; England said he is heading to the North Sea and does not want trouble in Norway/Sweden. Germany was openly pushy, said he will move to Prussia and told me not to interfere; he never gave a clear assurance on Sweden, so assume A BER-PRU and possible northern awkwardness. Austria gave mixed signals: first floated A VIE-GAL, then agreed to a Galicia DMZ and said he would focus south; treat the DMZ as possible but not fully reliable. Turkey agreed to a Black Sea DMZ and no Armenia, says he plans Bulgaria and wants a long-term RT arrangement; warm tone but still verify by moves. Italy expects Austria/Turkey tension in the southeast and is open to information-sharing. No meaningful contact with France.
Intent: Current S1901M plan is to honor the England understanding and likely honor the Turkey understanding for now: F STP/SC-BOT for Sweden, A WAR-UKR as a southern hedge while respecting a Galicia DMZ, A MOS-STP to keep northern flexibility, F SEV H because of the Black Sea DMZ. I intend to fulfill the England Norway/Sweden arrangement. I currently intend to fulfill the Turkey Black Sea DMZ this spring, but only provisionally pending his actual move. I intend to respect a Galicia DMZ, but Austria's earlier GAL talk means I am watching closely and will react hard if he enters Galicia. Germany is not trusted; do not concede more than necessary in the north and remember he declared Prussia in advance.

[S1901M] Austria broke faith immediately by moving VIE-GAL after talking DMZ; that is the clearest betrayal and must shape all future dealings with him. Germany did exactly what he advertised and tried BER-PRU; my WAR-PRU bounce was important, both to stop him entering Prussia and to show I will not be pushed around in the north. England kept the northern understanding in spirit: no move against Sweden/Norway arrangements and no direct anti-Russian action. Turkey also honored the Black Sea/Armenia understanding this turn, which slightly improves his credibility. My own moves were more assertive than the earlier draft plan: MOS-UKR and SEV-RUM secured a strong southern foothold while BOT preserves the Sweden plan. Net result: good tactical position, but Austria in Galicia creates immediate danger to Ukraine/Rumania/Warsaw and may force an anti-Austrian response.

[F1901M] England reaffirmed the Norway-for-England, Sweden-for-Russia understanding and remains committed to a quiet north; no sign of English hostility. Germany said he will not contest Sweden this fall, but his tone stayed coercive: he demanded I withdraw from Prussia/Ukraine/Rumania and explicitly threatened coordinated pressure with Austria and Turkey, so his Sweden promise should be treated cautiously. Austria is the clearest current enemy: he already broke the Galicia DMZ in spring, then tried to excuse it as a precaution. He now says GAL will not move to WAR or UKR this turn and may move back west/defensive, but this is not trustworthy; assume any Austrian promise can be false. Turkey did honor the spring Black Sea/Armenia calm, but is now uneasy about my fleet in Rumania, says Austria and Germany are courting him, and asked for concrete concessions such as support to Greece or a Ukraine pullback; no deal was reached, and there is no firm southern agreement beyond my conditional offer of mutual non-pressure if he keeps BLA and BUL off me. Italy remains useful for information-sharing and may exploit Austrian overextension later. No meaningful contact with France. Key board memory: Austria's GAL move was the major betrayal, Germany tried PRU and was bounced, England kept the northern spirit, and Turkey was honest in spring but is now wavering.
Intent: Primary committed move is F BOT-SWE; I intend to fulfill the England understanding and secure Sweden while avoiding any move against England. I have not made any concrete concession to Turkey or Austria and do not intend to. If Germany truly leaves Sweden and the Baltic alone, I am willing to avoid a northern escalation this turn, but I do not trust him and will not concede leverage. Main operational priority is the south: preserve Rumania if possible, contain or punish Austria's Galicia army, and avoid letting GAL dictate my WAR/UKR/RUM posture. Southern orders should be defensive-first and anti-Austrian, with only conditional calm toward Turkey if he shows it by action.

[F1901M] England again proved the most reliable partner: he took Norway and left Sweden for me, so the northern understanding held and I finished 1901 on 6 centers. Germany did not contest Sweden, but his moves to Prussia and Silesia confirm he remains coercive and dangerous; any calm with him is only temporary. Austria stayed openly hostile, using Serbia and Galicia against Rumania. My A WAR-GAL was the right call: even though it bounced, it cut Austrian support and, with UKR supporting, saved Rumania. The bigger disappointment was Turkey. After earlier calm, he moved to Black Sea, sent Ankara to Armenia, and supported the Austrian attack on Rumania, showing he is now willing to join anti-Russian pressure. Main lesson: keep attacking Galicia, trust England most, and treat Austria-Turkey coordination as a real immediate threat.

[S1902M] England fully reaffirmed the Norway-for-England, Sweden-for-Russia understanding and promised no pressure on StP/SWE; this is the only firm reliable agreement and should be preserved. Italy remained cooperative, said he is preparing pressure on TRI/VIE, and wants continued intelligence-sharing against Austria. Turkey admitted Austria is pushing him into a full anti-Russian attack and asked for concrete compensation; no deal was reached. My standing offer to Turkey was simple non-hostility this spring if he does not move/support against RUM or pressure SEV from ARM, but I should assume hostility unless his moves prove otherwise. Germany was openly hostile and threatening, claiming Austria and Turkey are committed and that WAR will fall; treat Germany as an active enemy. France was receptive to information-sharing about German overextension but made no commitments. Key memory for orders: only England deal is firm; Italy is useful but not committed tactically; Turkey is probing but untrusted; Germany is explicitly hostile; Austria remains the primary southeastern enemy after the Galicia betrayal.
Intent: I intend to honor the England agreement fully this spring: no move against Norway and no northern provocation from SWE unless Germany creates an emergency. No other firm agreement binds me. I do not intend to meet Turkey's demand for concrete territorial concessions, and I do not trust his hints at a deal without visible proof on the board. Main operational intent is defensive and anti-Austrian/anti-German: assume possible coordinated pressure on WAR and RUM from Germany/Austria/Turkey, prioritize preserving Warsaw and contesting/holding Rumania as far as tactically possible, and use moves that cut enemy supports or keep Galicia from dictating the board. Continue coordinating politically with Italy against Austria and sharing anti-German information with England and France.

[S1902M] England’s reliability collapsed this turn: after explicitly promising no pressure on StP/SWE, he stabbed with NWY-STP/NC and covered with NWG-NWY. I kept my word in the north, so this was a clean betrayal and means England can no longer be treated as a trusted partner. Germany also did exactly as threatened, attacking WAR from SIL with PRU support; only MOS support kept Warsaw alive. In the south, Austria and Turkey again coordinated hard against Rumania, and ARM cut SEV’s support as expected, but UKR-GAL successfully cut Austrian help and the Austro-Turk attacks bounced each other, so RUM survived. Italy was the one bright spot: VEN-TRI succeeded, finally putting real pressure on Austria’s rear. Main lesson: I am now facing a broad anti-Russian squeeze, and England must be reclassified from friend to opportunist.

[F1902M] No new binding agreements were reached. England cleanly stabbed into STP after explicit assurances; he now claims he does not intend immediate pressure on SWE/BAL and wants to avoid full northern war, but this is not trustworthy. Germany remained openly hostile, explicitly threatening a renewed PRU+SIL attack on WAR; no deal. Turkey was fully candid that he intends to take RUM this fall and offered only a ceasefire if I voluntarily vacate it; I rejected this and made no concession. Italy is the best current partner: he successfully took TRI, plans to keep pressure on VIE/BUD, and wants continued coordination and intel-sharing for an anti-Austrian push in 1903. France remains non-committal but receptive to intelligence about German eastern overcommitment; possible future diversion, no present promise. Key memory: broad anti-Russian squeeze is real; England is no longer reliable, Germany/Turkey/Austria are active enemies, Italy is useful, France is only a political prospect.
Intent: F1902 priorities are survival and damage control on all fronts. I do not intend to honor Turkey's demand for a voluntary withdrawal from RUM; I will try to hold or at least strongly contest RUM. I also intend to hold WAR against Germany, likely prioritizing MOS support if needed. In the north, I made no firm concession to England; despite his talk of restraint I will treat him as untrusted and focus on preventing any follow-up loss of SWE/BAL while avoiding unnecessary northern overextension if possible. I intend to continue practical coordination with Italy against Austria and continued intelligence-sharing with France about German exposure. Only soft commitment I may still keep is not launching a gratuitous anti-English attack if England truly stops at STP, but I will absolutely defend SWE and my northern position.

[F1902M] F1902 confirmed the anti-Russian bloc and cost me Rumania. Germany renewed the PRU/SIL attack on Warsaw exactly as threatened; only support from MOS and UKR kept WAR alive. Austria and Turkey again coordinated effectively: ARM cut SEV, BUL supported BLA into RUM, and Austria added GAL/SER support, dislodging my fleet and likely costing the center. England stayed hostile with NWY-SWE, but BAL bounced him and he gained nothing further in the north. The other major setback was Italy’s failure: his move on VIE did not break Austria, and Austria immediately retook TRI with BUD supported by VIE, reducing pressure on my best potential ally’s front. Main lesson: Germany/Austria/Turkey are acting as a real operational alliance, England remains opportunistic, and survival now depends on holding WAR/SWE while finding a way to re-stabilize the south.

[S1903M] No binding peace deals were reached. France is the main new opportunity: he says he is striking Germany this spring with A HOL->KIE and A BUR->MUN or A BEL->RUH, and asked me to apply eastern pressure and keep this confidential. I did not promise reckless attacks, but I did signal Germany would not get a free spring in the east. Italy remains cooperative and says A TYR will pressure VIE, A ALB will pressure SER, and fleets will secure ADR/ION; however I did not confirm any exact Russian move into BUD and made clear WAR security comes first, so this is soft coordination only. England offered no real de-escalation after the STP stab; I told him only proof matters and demanded he stay out of SWE/BOT/BAL, with no concessions from me. Turkey explicitly declared he intends to take SEV and offered only a promise-based ceasefire if I yield it; I refused, so assume full Turkish hostility. Germany explicitly said he is attacking WAR again this spring; assume renewed PRU/SIL pressure. Key board-read to remember: Germany, Austria, and Turkey remain the active anti-Russian bloc; England is still opportunistic and dangerous but not yet part of a formal coordinated deal this turn; France and Italy are the only useful counterweights.
Intent: Primary intent is still survival with WAR the top priority. I do not intend to honor any Turkish demand to concede SEV, but in practice I likely cannot save both WAR and SEV; WAR remains more important. I made no binding exact-move promise to France or Italy, only a soft commitment that Germany will not get a free spring and that Austria/GAL will stay under strain if possible. Current likely order concept: A WAR H, A MOS S A WAR, A UKR->GAL to keep Austria tied down/cut support, and F BAL->BER or otherwise directly pressure Germany from the Baltic; this would fulfill the soft anti-German understanding with France without gambling WAR. I do not intend any voluntary northern concession to England; if England stays out of SWE/BOT/BAL, fine, but I am trusting only board proof.

[S1903M] Spring 1903 confirmed the board lines clearly. Germany did exactly what he said: PRU-SIL pressure on WAR again, but MOS support kept WAR alive, which was the right priority. Turkey also carried out his threat exactly, taking SEV with ARM supported by RUM and re-entering BLA from ANK; no trust remains there. England gave the clearest northern proof of hostility by moving into SWE, so any hope of de-escalation is dead.

On the positive side, France fully honored his anti-German plan, taking KIE and MUN, which is the biggest strategic bright spot. Italy also broadly followed through by pressuring VIE/SER and securing ADR, even if no Austrian break occurred. My own BAL-PRU failed because BER covered, and UKR-GAL only bounced. Lesson: WAR defense worked, but I am now stretched to the brink and must exploit French pressure immediately.

[F1903M] France fully honored the anti-German spring plan by taking KIE and MUN and now wants F1903 A KIE->BER supported by A MUN, asking me to cut German support with F BAL->PRU or A WAR->SIL. I gave no binding order promise, only that I would deny Germany a free hand if possible without risking WAR. Italy remains cooperative against Austria, saying he is pushing TRI and then SER/GRE; I agreed only in principle to keep Austria tied down and made no exact tactical commitment because WAR defense comes first. England provided no de-escalation and has now proven northern hostility by taking SWE. Turkey openly threatened SEV, then took it with support, so there is no live peace track there. Key memory: no binding peace or alliance deals were reached this round; France is the one power that actually did what he said on the board.
Intent: Primary intent for F1903 is still survival with WAR first. Default order concept is conservative-but-active: keep WAR defended, most likely with A MOS supporting A WAR, avoid any voluntary concession to Turkey or England, and if tactically safe use F BAL aggressively against PRU to help cut German support for France's BER attack. I do not currently intend to fulfill France's riskier suggestion of A WAR->SIL unless late evidence makes WAR clearly safe. A UKR move is intended either to keep pressure on GAL or, if German/Austrian coordination still looks dangerous, to add further defense to WAR instead of gambling. I made no promise to honor Germany's request that I not exploit his western crisis; if a safe anti-German move exists, I intend to take it.

[F1903M] F1903 confirmed that WAR-first was still correct: Germany did not hit WAR after all, but Austria immediately cut UKR support with GAL-UKR, so relaxing defense would have been dangerous. My BAL-PRU succeeded because Germany vacated, giving me useful forward position without risking WAR. The biggest surprise was France: after proposing KIE->BER with MUN support, he instead shifted to RUH and did not strike BER, whether by change of plan or failed coordination. Germany clearly pivoted west, moving SIL->MUN and PRU->LVN; his “no attack on WAR” claim was true this turn, but LVN keeps pressure alive, so no trust restored. Italy’s retake of TRI is the best southern news and keeps Austria stretched. England consolidated DEN/SWE rather than pushing farther east; still hostile, just cautious. Turkey’s supported hold in SEV confirms he intends to keep my south permanently.

[S1904M] No binding deals were reached. France remains the most useful partner and wants to finish Germany with A KIE->BER and A BUR->MUN supported by A RUH; important reminder: France was initially working from an outdated board and asked for F PRU support, but that fleet was disbanded, so I explicitly did not promise any exact help beyond interfering with Germany if it can be done without exposing WAR. Italy continues friendly anti-Austrian coordination, asking me to keep pressure on GAL/BUD while he presses ALB/GRE/SER/VIE; I gave only conditional support and no exact order promise because WAR security comes first. England says he wants to focus west against France and claims he has no desire to spend more effort in the east if I do not act against his current holdings; treat this as possible temporary de-escalation only, not trust. Austria refused the key proof I demanded, namely vacating GAL; instead he floated anti-Italy/France cooperation and claimed he would show peace by not moving GAL->WAR/UKR this spring, which I did not accept as sufficient. Net takeaway: France and Italy are still the only useful counterweights, but with only A WAR and A MOS left, survival comes first and no one has earned enough trust to justify exposing Warsaw.
Intent: Primary S1904M intent is still WAR-first survival with active defense rather than passive holding. Default plan is to keep Austria from having a free shot from GAL while preserving WAR, most likely with A WAR->GAL and A MOS->WAR. I made no binding order commitments to anyone. I do not intend to honor Germany's request to freeze the east, and I do not intend to join Austria's anti-Italy/France line. I also do not currently intend to fulfill France's riskier anti-German idea via a WAR move toward SIL/PRU, because that would open Warsaw unless Austria proves restraint on the board; only if late evidence makes WAR clearly safe would I consider a stronger anti-German interference move instead.

[S1904M] My WAR-first active defense was correct: A WAR-GAL bounced and, crucially, cut Austria’s support for Turkey’s SEV->UKR move, keeping WAR secure and proving again that passive defense would have been worse. Austria did not give the board-proof restraint I wanted; instead he stayed in GAL and visibly coordinated with Turkey. Turkey executed a strong southern rotation anyway, ending with UKR/SEV/BLA pressure intact and the southern threat still severe. England’s talk of eastern de-escalation was only partially borne out: he made no new direct move against me, but he openly supported Germany back into KIE, showing he is still willing to strengthen my enemies when useful. France failed to carry out the hoped-for anti-German pressure and lost KIE, so western relief weakened. Italy kept fighting but Austria/Turkey gained in the Ionian. No promises were broken by me because I made none.

[F1904M] No binding agreements were made. Austria suddenly claimed Turkey stabbed him and proposed a RU-A truce built around A GAL->UKR with Russian support, but he still refused the only proof that matters: vacating GAL first. Treat this as opportunistic and untrusted. France again pushed for anti-German cooperation and specifically asked for A WAR->SIL to help finish Germany, claiming Italy would keep GAL occupied; I did not agree because GAL is still occupied and WAR cannot be exposed on promises. Germany again asked for an eastern freeze and explicitly said to let Turkey handle the south; I rejected this and noted that only board-proof restraint matters. Italy remained the most cooperative southern partner, urging continued pressure on Austria; I encouraged him to keep Austrian units tied down but gave no exact move commitment. Turkey was fully explicit that he does not intend to ease pressure and even suggested I concede WAR for a temporary reprieve; this was rejected and confirms total hostility. Key board lesson from spring must be remembered: active anti-GAL defense in S1904 cut support and saved WAR, but with both GAL and UKR now adjacent in fall, pure activity may no longer be board-safe if it risks a supported capture of WAR.
Intent: Primary intent for F1904M is still WAR-first survival, now with the strongest board-safe defense as the default. Unless a clearly safe tactical change appears at order entry, plan is A WAR H and A MOS S A WAR to prevent a supported GAL/UKR capture. I made no binding commitments and do not intend to fulfill France's requested A WAR->SIL, Austria's requested support for GAL->UKR, Germany's proposed freeze, or Turkey's demand that I concede WAR. If late board reading shows one of GAL or UKR is clearly neutralized, I can reconsider a more active anti-GAL/anti-German move, but default is full defense of Warsaw.

[F1904M] No binding deals existed, so no promises were broken by me or clearly by anyone else. My WAR-first defense was still correct: MOS support was cut by Turkey’s UKR->MOS, but because neither Austria nor Turkey actually attacked WAR, both of my centers survived. The most important tactical detail is that Austria’s GAL->UKR and Turkey’s UKR->MOS bounced head-to-head, showing at minimum failed A/T coordination and possibly the first real crack between them, though both remain enemies until proven otherwise. Austria still gave no meaningful proof of peace by staying in GAL. Italy provided the best news by winning ION and cutting Austrian support, keeping pressure on Vienna’s flank. In the west, England again avoided direct anti-Russian action but weakened my best counterweight by taking BEL from France; France at least retook KIE and kept Germany on the ropes.

[S1905M] No binding agreements were made with anyone. Austria publicly called for an anti-Turkey coalition and privately kept pushing for A GAL->UKR with Russian support from WAR, but I rejected this again: no trust or cooperation while GAL remains adjacent to WAR, and no acceptance of promise-based anti-T talk without board-proof restraint. France publicly endorsed anti-T containment and privately again asked for WAR->SIL or WAR->PRU to help finish Germany; I declined because GAL and UKR both still threaten Warsaw. Germany repeated its request for an eastern freeze and specifically claimed planned orders A BER->KIE with A MUN S A BER->KIE; I made no promise, only said I would judge board-proof restraint. Italy remains the best partner: he says he is independently pushing hard at ALB/GRE and keeping Austria/Turkey tied down; I encouraged this and shared that Turkey explicitly wants Moscow. England says he is focused west and does not want further eastern expansion if I do not threaten his holdings; this is only possible temporary de-escalation, not trust. Turkey was fully hostile and explicit: he demanded I give up Moscow, suggested WAR->GAL or even WAR supporting UKR->MOS, and tried extortion; all rejected. Key message to future self: do not be lured by Austria's and France's anti-T rhetoric into freeing WAR while GAL still sits there and UKR/SEV pressure remains live.
Intent: WAR-first survival remains the plan for S1905M. No move agreements were accepted, and I do not intend to fulfill Austria's request for WAR S GAL->UKR, France's request for WAR->SIL/PRU, Germany's requested freeze as a promise, or any Turkish proposal involving conceding MOS, WAR->GAL, or WAR S UKR->MOS. Default order set is A WAR H and A MOS S A WAR as the strongest board-safe defense against a possible GAL+UKR attack on Warsaw. Only deviate if last-second board reading shows a clearly safe tactic that still keeps WAR secure.

[S1905M] Spring 1905 confirmed that promises still mean nothing without board proof. I made no commitments and broke none. My conservative defense kept both centers alive: UKR’s attack cut MOS support, but because Austria did not join a direct strike on WAR, Warsaw survived. Austria’s anti-Turkey talk remains unproven and likely opportunistic; GAL stayed active next to Warsaw and even tried to shift to UKR instead of giving visible restraint. Turkey stayed fully hostile with UKR->MOS and continued locking down the south by supporting SEV and consolidating fleets. The only possible crack is that Austria and Turkey still failed to produce a clean coordinated result, but that is not yet trustable. Germany did tell the truth about BER->KIE with MUN support, and England helped from DEN, dislodging France from KIE and weakening my best western counterweight. Lesson: WAR-first caution was correct.

[F1905M] No binding agreements were made with anyone. Austria again tried to recruit me into an anti-Turkey line, specifically pushing WAR support for GAL->UKR and even MOS->SEV, claiming GAL->UKR would be 'proof' and that GAL would later vacate; I rejected this and reiterated that only actually vacating GAL and easing pressure on WAR/MOS counts as proof. Turkey offered a 'survival pact': he says UKR will stop attacking MOS or hold if I use WAR against Austria/GAL, or alternatively that we can both hold; I rejected all promise-based versions and stated I will not free WAR unless UKR/SEV/BLA pressure visibly eases on the board. France again wanted pressure or at least hints toward PRU/SIL to distract Germany, but accepted that my survival comes first; I passed along useful intel that Turkey is trying to peel me away from Austria and noted England's continuing northern growth. Germany repeated a truce line and warned me not to test PRU/SIL; I gave no promise, only said I judge calm by visible board restraint. Italy remains the best partner: he says he will keep pressing the TRI-ALB-GRE-SER corridor and the ION/AEG axis, and I encouraged that while sharing that Turkey is feeling southern pressure. England says he has no reason to expand further east if I stay passive, but I made no deal and do not trust assurances without board proof.
Intent: WAR-first survival remains the plan for F1905M. No moves were agreed to, and I do not intend to fulfill Austria's request for WAR S GAL->UKR or MOS->SEV, France's request for movement or hints toward PRU/SIL, Germany's implied freeze as a promise, or Turkey's request for WAR->GAL / support against Austria / any promise-based de-escalation. Default intended orders are A WAR H and A MOS S A WAR as the strongest board-safe defense against a possible GAL+UKR strike on Warsaw. Only deviate if there is last-second visible board-proof change that removes the GAL/UKR threat without risking WAR.

[F1905M] Fall 1905 again proved that caution was correct. I made no promises and broke none; WAR H with MOS support kept both centers safe. The big board fact was a visible Austria-Turkey clash: GAL->UKR and UKR->GAL bounced, and Austria’s ALB->GRE also failed against Turkish support. That is stronger evidence of a crack than mere rhetoric, though not yet a reason to trust either side while GAL still threatens Warsaw and Turkish fleets still lock down the south. In the west, England actively helped Germany survive by supporting KIE->HOL, which hurt France, my best anti-German counterweight. Italy achieved little this turn; his attempted ALB action failed and southern pressure did not grow. Lesson: keep prioritizing WAR-first survival, watch for real Austro-Turkish fracture, encourage Italy and France, and never relax simply because enemies start fighting each other.

[S1906M] No binding agreements were made with anyone. Austria again pushed anti-Turkey coordination, first asking for WAR and MOS to support GAL->UKR, then offering board-proof by vacating GAL with GAL->BUD supported by VIE; I did not confirm any follow-up support and repeated that only an actually empty GAL counts as proof. Turkey claims UKR->GAL with RUM support and says he has no orders against WAR or MOS; I gave no promise and told him I will judge only by adjudicated board proof. France again urged a WAR->SIL or PRU feint against Germany; I declined because WAR remains too exposed. Germany asked for calm and claimed fully western orders BER->KIE, HOL->BUR, MUN support; I made no promise. England says his focus is west and he does not intend further eastern expansion if undisturbed; no deal was made. Italy remains the best partner and says he is pressing ALB/GRE and the ION/AEG axis; I encouraged maximum pressure and shared that Turkey claims to be turning on Austria. Key fact for future self: there may be a real Austria-Turkey clash over GAL this turn, but do not trust either side until the board shows sustained restraint and WAR is genuinely safer.
Intent: I agreed to nothing and do not intend to fulfill Austria's requests for Russian support, France's request for WAR->SIL/PRU, Germany's request for a promised freeze, or any Turkish request for relaxed defense or non-interference. S1906M intent remains WAR-first survival. Default orders are A WAR H and A MOS S A WAR as the safest anti-surprise defense. A WAL will move to pressure the French heartland (likely BUR). F STP and F BOT will hold or maneuver to secure the North and maintain a presence in the Baltic as a distraction for Russia.

[S1906M] The coordinated strike with Germany was a success, effectively seizing KIE and pushing Germany into RUH. My Atlantic push also succeeded, capturing MAO and cutting French support. France continues to "turtle" in the heartland (BUR, PIC, BRE), but their perimeter is collapsing. Turkey remains a powerhouse, dismantling Austria and pressuring Italy, which keeps the southern flank secure.

I must now coordinate with Germany to transition from perimeter pressure to a decisive strike on Paris and Burgundy.

I will move A YOR -> BUR to maintain pressure on the French heartland. In the North, I will move F STP/NC -> BOT to pressure Russia, F FIN -> STP to secure the center, and F DEN -> NTH to reposition.

full_private_diary:
[S1901M] England: Agreed DMZ in ENG; I will move F BRE to MAO, they will keep fleet out of ENG. Discussed cooperation against Germany and division of Low Countries; I proposed taking Belgium, they may take Holland or Norway. Germany: Agreed to avoid conflict in Burgundy; I will move A PAR to PIC, not BUR. Germany claims focus is East, no interest in West; I indicated I want Belgium, they did not object. Italy: Agreed non-aggression pact, no moves to PIE; I will move A MAR to Spain. Italy focuses on central Med and Balkans, open to future coordination against Germany.
Intent: Execute agreed moves: F BRE -> MAO, A MAR -> Spain, A PAR -> Picardy. This secures Iberia and positions for Belgium in fall, honoring all non-aggression and DMZ agreements.

[S1901M] All three moves succeeded as planned: F MAO, A SPA, A PIC. England kept the DMZ—their fleet stayed out of the Channel. Germany avoided Burgundy entirely, and Italy respected our non-aggression pact. No betrayals this phase; all agreements were honored. Our position is excellent: we’re poised to take Portugal and Belgium in the fall, which should give us three builds. The only potential competition for Belgium is England via convoy, but that’s unlikely given their focus on Norway. Russia’s bounce in Prussia with Germany may distract both eastward. For now, England, Germany, and Italy remain trustworthy, but I’ll watch for any shift in German ambitions toward the Low Countries. Next step: F MAO to POR, A PIC to BEL, and consider A SPA supporting or holding to secure Iberia.

[F1901M] England confirmed continued DMZ in the Channel, supports France taking Belgium, and is moving to Norway. Germany reaffirmed non-aggression and will not contest Belgium, likely moving on Holland. Italy confirmed Piedmont non-aggression, focusing on Tunis, open to future coordination. All Spring agreements were honored without betrayal, and all powers remain cooperative.
Intent: Move F MAO to Portugal. Move A PIC to Belgium. Hold A SPA in Spain to secure Iberia.

[F1901M] All agreements honored flawlessly. England respected the Channel DMZ, taking Norway and moving an army to Wales—an odd choice that demands scrutiny. Germany stuck to non-aggression, vacating Denmark and ignoring Holland, leaving both centers neutral. Their fleet in Helgoland Bight is benign for now. Italy remained calm in Piedmont, securing Tunis. Our taking of Belgium and Portugal with a held Spain grants us three builds and a dominant 6-center position. England’s army in Wales is a potential threat if combined with a future Channel fleet, but for now the DMZ holds. Germany’s passive play makes them a tempting target for eastward expansion. Trust in England, Germany, and Italy remains intact, but I’ll monitor Wales and continue diplomatic charm. Build priorities: armies for a Low Countries bulge, possibly a fleet in Brest to secure the Atlantic. Next phase, coordinate with allies and consider a push into Germany.

[S1902M] Germany agreed to let France take Holland with A BEL, moving their fleet to North Sea (NTH) and focusing east; in return, France will not move on Kiel or Munich. England continues to respect the Channel DMZ; France expressed concern about England's army in Wales and shared intel on Germany's planned NTH move, but no concrete coordination was agreed. Italy formally reaffirmed the non-aggression pact regarding Piedmont, with both sides respecting spheres of influence. Russia provided intelligence on Germany's eastward posture and remains open to information exchange, with no specific agreements made.
Intent: Honor the agreement with Germany: move A BEL to HOL. Cover Belgium by moving A PAR to PIC. Reposition defensively by moving A MAR to BUR. Hold A SPA and F POR to secure Iberia. Move F BRE to MAO to strengthen Atlantic presence without violating the Channel DMZ. All moves are consistent with existing pacts and non-aggression commitments.

[S1902M] Diary Entry – Spring 1902 Moves (S1902M)

All my moves succeeded: took Holland as agreed with Germany, consolidated Picardy and Burgundy, and repositioned the fleet to MAO. Germany honored its side—fleet tried for North Sea, army pushed toward Warsaw—but both bounced (England contested NTH, Russia held Warsaw). No betrayal. England kept the Channel DMZ but moved LON to NTH, likely responding to my tip about German plans. That bounce sowed Anglo-German discord, which I can exploit. Italy took Trieste but botched the Ionian, remaining friendly. Belgium is uncovered but safe for now; I’ll need A PIC to cover it in Fall. Strategic lesson: My position is solid, but the empty Belgium is a vulnerability. In Fall, I should secure Belgium while keeping options open for a stab east or north once Anglo-German friction escalates. Germany remains trustworthy; England not hostile, but watchful.

[F1902M] Germany agreed to non-aggression: we keep west of Rhine and away from Kiel/Munich; they move fleet to Denmark to focus east. England respects Channel DMZ and has no issue with us taking Belgium, but they bounced with Germany in NTH. Italy reaffirmed Piedmont pact. Russia continues to provide intel on German eastern overcommitment and urges us to strike, but we are not yet ready. Belgium is vacant and we plan to take it this fall, as communicated to all.
Intent: Move A PIC to BEL with support from A HOL. Hold A BUR, A SPA, F POR, and F MAO. This secures Belgium without violating any pacts (no moves into Ruhr or Channel). Maintain defensive posture to keep England and Germany calm, while setting up for potential offensive in 1903.

[F1902M] Diary Entry – Fall 1902 Moves (F1902M)

Belgium secured as planned: A PIC moved to BEL with support from A HOL. No betrayals—Germany honored non-aggression by moving fleet to Denmark, England kept Channel DMZ. However, England now has F NTH and A WAL, a concerning buildup that could threaten the Channel if trust erodes. Germany remains weak (only 3 centers) and fully committed east, bouncing off Warsaw. Italy moved A VEN to TYR, bordering my A BUR; still friendly but worth watching. Russia lost Rumania to Turkey, weakening their southern front. My position is solid with 6 centers and a compact line from Iberia to the Low Countries. Strategic lesson: Belgium is now safe, but I must build armies in winter to exploit German vulnerability in 1903, while keeping a fleet in MAO to deter England. The Anglo-German friction in North Sea is a gift—I can let them bleed each other while I push toward Munich or the Ruhr.

[S1903M] Russia confirms Germany is overextended eastward and encourages hitting KIE and MUN, promising eastern pressure but no guaranteed support. Italy pledges zero movement into MUN or Low Countries, fully supporting our German campaign. England remains open to extended non-aggression but has not formalized; DMZ still honored. Germany is deceived into believing we are friendly and focused on Russia. All pacts with other powers intact.
Intent: Spring 1903 moves: A HOL → KIE, A BUR → MUN, A BEL hold, A PAR → BUR, A SPA → GAS, F POR hold, F MAO hold. This seizes exposed German centers while keeping Belgium secure and backfilling Burgundy. Western reserves begin shifting east.

[S1903M] Executed Spring 1903 plan flawlessly: A HOL → KIE and A BUR → MUN both succeeded, capturing both German centers. A BEL held, A PAR → BUR backfilled, A SPA → GAS shifted east, F MAO supported, F POR held. Germany is now reduced to BER and DEN, with their eastern offensive bouncing in PRU and WAR. No betrayals: Italy honored non-aggression, moving A TYR → VIE (bounce) and staying clear of MUN; England kept Channel DMZ; Russia held WAR and supported, though failed to coordinate a direct strike on PRU. Austria and Italy clashed in TYR and SER, distracting both. Turkey advanced in SEV. Our position is dominant: 7 centers, two new German gains, compact line from Iberia to Kiel. Germany is finished; we must secure KIE/MUN against any desperate counter, then push for BER or DEN. Maintain English and Italian trust, but watch Italy’s TYR presence. Russia remains friendly but may demand spoils; coordinate to finish Germany quickly.

[F1903M] England: Channel DMZ holds, we offered Denmark but no formal acceptance; they remain friendly but watchful. Russia: supportive, will try to cut German support in east but no specific move promised; we agreed to attack Berlin. Italy: reaffirmed non-aggression, focused on Balkans. Germany: hostile, threatening to retake Kiel and Munich.
Intent: Attack Berlin with A KIE -> BER supported by A MUN. Protect MUN with A BUR support A MUN. Move A BEL -> RUH to threaten Kiel and cover if needed. Hold A GAS, F POR, F MAO. This fulfills our promise to Russia to pressure Berlin while securing our gains.

[F1903M] Lost Munich to a German counterattack (A SIL → MUN supported by BER) while our A MUN was wasted on a void support for Austria. A KIE’s support for RUH was cut by F HEL, but A BEL → RUH still succeeded. England seized Denmark, expanding to 8 centers and tightening its Baltic grip. Russia took Prussia, now bordering our Kiel. Our failure to attack Berlin as promised to Russia may strain that relationship. Italy honored our alliance, focusing on Austria. We hold 7 centers, no build. Critical lesson: never leave a key center undefended with a speculative support; coordinate moves with actual allied actions. England’s growth and naval presence demand vigilance—Channel DMZ holds but their Baltic fleet is a future threat. Must retake Munich or push for Berlin next year, while reinforcing Kiel against possible Russian or English pressure. Shift western reserves eastward urgently.

[S1904M] England remains friendly, Channel DMZ intact. Italy reaffirmed absolute non-aggression in west, focusing on Balkans. Russia cannot support from Prussia (fleet disbanded), but we formally asked them to support A KIE→BER with A WAR; they indicated they will choose strongest interference without endangering Warsaw, likely support. Germany threatened to retake Kiel but is weak. Planned coordinated attack on BER and MUN with Russian aid.
Intent: Spring 1904M orders: A KIE → BER (seek Russia's A WAR S A KIE → BER), A BUR → MUN, A RUH S A BUR → MUN, A GAS → BUR, A PAR → GAS, A MAR hold, F POR hold, F MAO hold. Request Russian support via message. Maintain Channel DMZ, no fleet into ECH. Shift western reserves eastward.

[S1904M] A devastating turn: our planned coordinated assault on Berlin and Munich was not executed — all French units held, likely due to a misorder (the orders submitted were all holds, not the intended moves). Germany capitalized immediately, retaking Kiel with A BER (supported by A MUN and England's F DEN). Our A KIE was dislodged and must retreat; Holland is the only viable option. Munich remains in German hands, and Berlin now sits empty but out of immediate reach.

Worse, England has betrayed the Channel DMZ: F LON moved to ENG, putting a hostile fleet directly off Brest. This, combined with their support for Germany in Kiel, signals a full shift to hostility. Russia’s A WAR bounced into Galicia, offering no support despite our request; they are unreliable.

Strategic impact: we lost Kiel, our German front is crumbling, and England threatens our northern coast. Italy remained consistent, moving into Apulia and the Tyrrhenian, but cannot directly counter England yet. We must retreat A KIE → HOL, rush A GAS to Brest to guard against English fleets, and urgently coordinate a counterstroke — likely A RUH → KIE with support from HOL, and A BUR toward MUN or BER. Our misorder cost us dearly; verify all submissions before finalizing. England is now a primary enemy; consider begging Italy for a distraction in the Mediterranean to pin English fleets.

[F1904M] Italy reaffirmed commitment to western neutrality and Balkan focus, refused naval help in west but assured Mediterranean dominance. Russia unable to move WAR west due to Austrian GAL threat, but will support indirectly if we pressure Germany and England. England broke Channel DMZ by moving into ENG, now hostile. Turkey's aggression stalls (lost GAL, ALB convoy failed). Austria pushing hard south vs their RUM/GRE/SEV. Russia/Italy: coordinate Balkans/Black Sea crush for shared gains. Germany/England/France: stable north, focus T elimination.

The lack of coordination in the last phase was a setback, but we can still deliver a decisive blow to France. I intend to put maximum pressure on the Atlantic coast and the Channel. What are your plans for A HOL and A KIE? I suggest we coordinate a concentrated strike on Paris and Burgundy to finally break their shell. Let me know your intended moves so we can synchronize.

Your dominance in the East is impressive and provides me with the security needed to focus entirely on dismantling France. I trust you have the situation with Russia and Italy well in hand. Let me know if you require any diplomatic support or if the balance of power shifts in your sector.

Kaiser, I note with interest your recent order supporting my advance into Ruhr. This suggests you see the futility of propping up England's dominance. I propose an immediate ceasefire and separate peace: I will withdraw from Ruhr and respect your sphere in the Low Countries if you break with England and turn your armies east. Together we can contain the English fleet. Let us discuss terms before this window closes.

Prime Minister, your ally Germany has betrayed you. Last season, Berlin ordered its armies to support my attack on Ruhr, deliberately undermining your position in Belgium. I have the orders to prove it. I am willing to negotiate a truce, but you must know you cannot trust the Kaiser. If you continue this war, you fight alone against a Germany that will stab you the moment it suits them.

Friend in Rome, the Anglo-German vice tightens. I am holding the line at Burgundy and Picardy, but any naval pressure you could apply in the Western Mediterranean—even a feint toward Spain or MAO—would draw English forces away from my coast. I do not ask for a commitment in the north, only a gesture to keep England honest. In return, I will support your interests in the Adriatic when the time comes.

England, your betrayal in F1906M cost us Ruhr. You hold Belgium now. We need to finish France before they recover. If you support A HOL -> BEL or A KIE -> DEN, we focus on France. If you block us, we take Belgium by force next turn. Choose wisely.
France, your position is untenable. We are regrouping in Munich and Holland. Surrender Belgium and Burgundy or face total annihilation. We will not stop until Paris falls.
Turkey, A BOH is adjacent to Munich. We are allies against Russia. Keep A BOH in Bohemia or move to SER. Do not threaten Munich, or we will cut your supply lines in the Balkans.
Russia, the truce holds. We will not move to Prussia or Silesia. Keep your units in Warsaw and Moscow. We need the East quiet to crush France.
Austria, stay in the Balkans. Do not move to Tyrol or Bohemia. We are handling the West. Focus on Italy and Turkey.

France, Italy reaffirms its absolute commitment to our western neutrality pact. You will see zero Italian movements toward PIE, TUS, or the western Mediterranean this turn. My focus remains entirely on the Balkan front against Austrian and Turkish overextension. Please continue your current posture; I will not interfere with your western operations, and I expect the same courtesy. A stable west allows me to dismantle the southern threats efficiently.

Germany, our friendly understanding remains intact. Italy will maintain strict neutrality in the west and north. I am directing all forces toward the Adriatic and Ionian seas to counter Austrian and Turkish expansion. If you continue to pressure Austria in Galicia and Bohemia, it will significantly ease my campaign in the Balkans. I appreciate your cooperation and will ensure my fleets never threaten your interests.

Russia, I am launching a coordinated naval-backed offensive to reclaim ALB and push into GRE, directly challenging Austrian and Turkish footholds. While I operate independently, our strategic interests temporarily align against southern expansion. Any pressure you apply on Galicia or the Black Sea will accelerate the collapse of our mutual rivals. I will maintain open channels as the board evolves.

The Mediterranean is entering a decisive phase. Italy is consolidating its naval dominance in the Ionian Sea to restore order and counter aggressive expansion by southern powers. All western powers can rest assured that Italian forces are strictly focused eastward. Any fleet moving west of the Aegean will be treated as a direct threat to regional stability.

You remain my most useful partner. From my side nothing has changed: I cannot free WAR while Austria sits in GAL and Turkey still has the whole SEV-BLA-RUM line behind it. If you can keep maximum pressure on the ALB/GRE/SER/VIE/BUD front and on the ION-AEG axis, that is the best help to me. If you see any concrete Austrian-Turkish split developing, send it over, but I am only treating adjudicated board proof as real.

Accurate eastern read from me: I am still in pure survival mode. Austria is back in GAL, so I am not freeing WAR for anti-German gestures. The immediate danger remains the Turkish position around SEV/BLA/RUM, with England still a long-term northern threat because of FIN plus held STP. If you can keep Germany under pressure and continue making England spend westward resources, that helps me far more than any request for WAR to wander.

Straight answer: while your army is in GAL, I cannot treat the east as safe and I will not expose WAR on assurances. If you want any future chance of practical cooperation, the proof is simple and on-board: GAL must stop threatening WAR and your moves must visibly run against Turkey, not through Russian space. I will judge by adjudication, not by promises.

Also straightforward from my side: I am not accepting promise-based calm while you still hold SEV and maintain BLA/RUM behind the line. If you want me to believe in any de-escalation, it has to appear on the board first. Until then I am assuming your position remains a direct threat to my last centers.

Critical opportunity this spring: My army is in Bohemia, directly threatening Vienna. If you move A MUN to Tyrolia, we can coordinate a devastating attack on Austria. Next turn, TYR supports BOH->VIE or BOH supports TYR->VIE - either way Vienna falls and Austria collapses completely. This eliminates a power that's been a thorn for both of us and opens up Italian centers for the taking. Would you be willing to send MUN->TYR this turn? I promise it's not a trick - I need Austria dead far more than I need anything from you.

Spring 1907 update: Despite a setback in Galicia (Austria reclaimed it), I now have A BOH threatening Vienna directly, plus F ALB positioned to hit Trieste or Serbia. I'm pressing Austria on multiple fronts simultaneously.

Could you encourage Germany to move MUN->TYR? If Germany threatens Vienna from the west while I attack from BOH, Austria cannot hold. Vienna falls this year with that coordination.

Also - Italy's F ION is blocking my fleet chain toward Naples/Tunis. Any diplomatic pressure you can apply on Italy to cooperate or at least redirect would help. How goes the campaign against France? You're doing magnificently from what I can see.

I want to point out something important: my army retreated from Galicia to BOHEMIA - moving further away from your borders, not closer. Austria has reclaimed GAL with their army. I am now focused entirely on taking Vienna.

Here's something that benefits us both: Austria's A GAL borders both Warsaw AND Vienna. Austria is a mutual enemy - their GAL army threatens you as much as it blocks me.

I have absolutely no designs on Moscow or Warsaw. My war is against Austria and Italy. Period.

Austria has A VEN sitting on YOUR supply center and will likely try to take Trieste back from you. Meanwhile my F ALB is positioned to take TRI myself. Here's a pragmatic offer: coordinate against Austria with me. You defend/retake VEN, I take TRI and SER. We both gain at Austria's expense rather than fighting each other while Austria profits.

Alternatively, if you move F ION out of my way voluntarily, I'll commit to not targeting Naples or Rome this year. You keep your 3 centers, I focus entirely on Austrian territory. Your choice - but refusing everything hasn't been working well for you strategically.

You played Galicia well last turn - credit where due. But now I'm in Bohemia threatening Vienna directly, with fleets closing in from the south. You're fighting on too many fronts: me from the east, Italy contesting Trieste, potentially Germany from the north.

Last offer: cede Serbia to me and I withdraw from Bohemia back east. You keep VIE, BUD, VEN, TUN. We establish a permanent border. Otherwise I coordinate with Germany for a joint attack on Vienna that you cannot survive. Your call.

Turkey, no Serbia cede—your BOH retreat failed gamble, now GAL/VIE 2v1 you there next if no pullback. Fleets south bounce forever. Cede GRE/ALB/RUM to me, withdraw BOH east, or face RU/GE/IT coordinated end. No Vienna threats work.
Germany, Balkans focus as requested—no TYR aggression. T's BOH menaces VIE, so VIE - BOH defensive (your MUN safe). Post-T, full FR support TYR/BOH S yours. Stable north, crush T together.
Turkey's overextension (BOH flop, ION stalls) cracks—Balkans/Black Sea powers unite: Austria GAL/SER vs RUM/GRE, Russia WAR/MOS vs UKR/SEV, Italy ION vs AEG. Shared gains vs their 7 SCs. West stable.

full_private_diary:
[S1901M] England agreed to a peaceful north: Norway for England, Sweden for Russia; England said he is heading to the North Sea and does not want trouble in Norway/Sweden. Germany was openly pushy, said he will move to Prussia and told me not to interfere; he never gave a clear assurance on Sweden, so assume A BER-PRU and possible northern awkwardness. Austria gave mixed signals: first floated A VIE-GAL, then agreed to a Galicia DMZ and said he would focus south; treat the DMZ as possible but not fully reliable. Turkey agreed to a Black Sea DMZ and no Armenia, says he plans Bulgaria and wants a long-term RT arrangement; warm tone but still verify by moves. Italy expects Austria/Turkey tension in the southeast and is open to information-sharing. No meaningful contact with France.
Intent: Current S1901M plan is to honor the England understanding and likely honor the Turkey understanding for now: F STP/SC-BOT for Sweden, A WAR-UKR as a southern hedge while respecting a Galicia DMZ, A MOS-STP to keep northern flexibility, F SEV H because of the Black Sea DMZ. I intend to fulfill the England Norway/Sweden arrangement. I currently intend to fulfill the Turkey Black Sea DMZ this spring, but only provisionally pending his actual move. I intend to respect a Galicia DMZ, but Austria's earlier GAL talk means I am watching closely and will react hard if he enters Galicia. Germany is not trusted; do not concede more than necessary in the north and remember he declared Prussia in advance.

[S1901M] Austria broke faith immediately by moving VIE-GAL after talking DMZ; that is the clearest betrayal and must shape all future dealings with him. Germany did exactly what he advertised and tried BER-PRU; my WAR-PRU bounce was important, both to stop him entering Prussia and to show I will not be pushed around in the north. England kept the northern understanding in spirit: no move against Sweden/Norway arrangements and no direct anti-Russian action. Turkey also honored the Black Sea/Armenia understanding this turn, which slightly improves his credibility. My own moves were more assertive than the earlier draft plan: MOS-UKR and SEV-RUM secured a strong southern foothold while BOT preserves the Sweden plan. Net result: good tactical position, but Austria in Galicia creates immediate danger to Ukraine/Rumania/Warsaw and may force an anti-Austrian response.

[F1901M] England reaffirmed the Norway-for-England, Sweden-for-Russia understanding and remains committed to a quiet north; no sign of English hostility. Germany said he will not contest Sweden this fall, but his tone stayed coercive: he demanded I withdraw from Prussia/Ukraine/Rumania and explicitly threatened coordinated pressure with Austria and Turkey, so his Sweden promise should be treated cautiously. Austria is the clearest current enemy: he already broke the Galicia DMZ in spring, then tried to excuse it as a precaution. He now says GAL will not move to WAR or UKR this turn and may move back west/defensive, but this is not trustworthy; assume any Austrian promise can be false. Turkey did honor the spring Black Sea/Armenia calm, but is now uneasy about my fleet in Rumania, says Austria and Germany are courting him, and asked for concrete concessions such as support to Greece or a Ukraine pullback; no deal was reached, and there is no firm southern agreement beyond my conditional offer of mutual non-pressure if he keeps BLA and BUL off me. Italy remains useful for information-sharing and may exploit Austrian overextension later. No meaningful contact with France. Key board memory: Austria's GAL move was the major betrayal, Germany tried PRU and was bounced, England kept the northern spirit, and Turkey was honest in spring but is now wavering.
Intent: Primary committed move is F BOT-SWE; I intend to fulfill the England understanding and secure Sweden while avoiding any move against England. I have not made any concrete concession to Turkey or Austria and do not intend to. If Germany truly leaves Sweden and the Baltic alone, I am willing to avoid a northern escalation this turn, but I do not trust him and will not concede leverage. Main operational priority is the south: preserve Rumania if possible, contain or punish Austria's Galicia army, and avoid letting GAL dictate my WAR/UKR/RUM posture. Southern orders should be defensive-first and anti-Austrian, with only conditional calm toward Turkey if he shows it by action.

[F1901M] England again proved the most reliable partner: he took Norway and left Sweden for me, so the northern understanding held and I finished 1901 on 6 centers. Germany did not contest Sweden, but his moves to Prussia and Silesia confirm he remains coercive and dangerous; any calm with him is only temporary. Austria stayed openly hostile, using Serbia and Galicia against Rumania. My A WAR-GAL was the right call: even though it bounced, it cut Austrian support and, with UKR supporting, saved Rumania. The bigger disappointment was Turkey. After earlier calm, he moved to Black Sea, sent Ankara to Armenia, and supported the Austrian attack on Rumania, showing he is now willing to join anti-Russian pressure. Main lesson: keep attacking Galicia, trust England most, and treat Austria-Turkey coordination as a real immediate threat.

[S1902M] England fully reaffirmed the Norway-for-England, Sweden-for-Russia understanding and promised no pressure on StP/SWE; this is the only firm reliable agreement and should be preserved. Italy remained cooperative, said he is preparing pressure on TRI/VIE, and wants continued intelligence-sharing against Austria. Turkey admitted Austria is pushing him into a full anti-Russian attack and asked for concrete compensation; no deal was reached. My standing offer to Turkey was simple non-hostility this spring if he does not move/support against RUM or pressure SEV from ARM, but I should assume hostility unless his moves prove otherwise. Germany was openly hostile and threatening, claiming Austria and Turkey are committed and that WAR will fall; treat Germany as an active enemy. France was receptive to information-sharing about German overextension but made no commitments. Key memory for orders: only England deal is firm; Italy is useful but not committed tactically; Turkey is probing but untrusted; Germany is explicitly hostile; Austria remains the primary southeastern enemy after the Galicia betrayal.
Intent: I intend to honor the England agreement fully this spring: no move against Norway and no northern provocation from SWE unless Germany creates an emergency. No other firm agreement binds me. I do not intend to meet Turkey's demand for concrete territorial concessions, and I do not trust his hints at a deal without visible proof on the board. Main operational intent is defensive and anti-Austrian/anti-German: assume possible coordinated pressure on WAR and RUM from Germany/Austria/Turkey, prioritize preserving Warsaw and contesting/holding Rumania as far as tactically possible, and use moves that cut enemy supports or keep Galicia from dictating the board. Continue coordinating politically with Italy against Austria and sharing anti-German information with England and France.

[S1902M] England’s reliability collapsed this turn: after explicitly promising no pressure on StP/SWE, he stabbed with NWY-STP/NC and covered with NWG-NWY. I kept my word in the north, so this was a clean betrayal and means England can no longer be treated as a trusted partner. Germany also did exactly as threatened, attacking WAR from SIL with PRU support; only MOS support kept Warsaw alive. In the south, Austria and Turkey again coordinated hard against Rumania, and ARM cut SEV’s support as expected, but UKR-GAL successfully cut Austrian help and the Austro-Turk attacks bounced each other, so RUM survived. Italy was the one bright spot: VEN-TRI succeeded, finally putting real pressure on Austria’s rear. Main lesson: I am now facing a broad anti-Russian squeeze, and England must be reclassified from friend to opportunist.

[F1902M] No new binding agreements were reached. England cleanly stabbed into STP after explicit assurances; he now claims he does not intend immediate pressure on SWE/BAL and wants to avoid full northern war, but this is not trustworthy. Germany remained openly hostile, explicitly threatening a renewed PRU+SIL attack on WAR; no deal. Turkey was fully candid that he intends to take RUM this fall and offered only a ceasefire if I voluntarily vacate it; I rejected this and made no concession. Italy is the best current partner: he successfully took TRI, plans to keep pressure on VIE/BUD, and wants continued coordination and intel-sharing for an anti-Austrian push in 1903. France remains non-committal but receptive to intelligence about German eastern overcommitment; possible future diversion, no present promise. Key memory: broad anti-Russian squeeze is real; England is no longer reliable, Germany/Turkey/Austria are active enemies, Italy is useful, France is only a political prospect.
Intent: F1902 priorities are survival and damage control on all fronts. I do not intend to honor Turkey's demand for a voluntary withdrawal from RUM; I will try to hold or at least strongly contest RUM. I also intend to hold WAR against Germany, likely prioritizing MOS support if needed. In the north, I made no firm concession to England; despite his talk of restraint I will treat him as untrusted and focus on preventing any follow-up loss of SWE/BAL while avoiding unnecessary northern overextension if possible. I intend to continue practical coordination with Italy against Austria and continued intelligence-sharing with France about German exposure. Only soft commitment I may still keep is not launching a gratuitous anti-English attack if England truly stops at STP, but I will absolutely defend SWE and my northern position.

[F1902M] F1902 confirmed the anti-Russian bloc and cost me Rumania. Germany renewed the PRU/SIL attack on Warsaw exactly as threatened; only support from MOS and UKR kept WAR alive. Austria and Turkey again coordinated effectively: ARM cut SEV, BUL supported BLA into RUM, and Austria added GAL/SER support, dislodging my fleet and likely costing the center. England stayed hostile with NWY-SWE, but BAL bounced him and he gained nothing further in the north. The other major setback was Italy’s failure: his move on VIE did not break Austria, and Austria immediately retook TRI with BUD supported by VIE, reducing pressure on my best potential ally’s front. Main lesson: Germany/Austria/Turkey are acting as a real operational alliance, England remains opportunistic, and survival now depends on holding WAR/SWE while finding a way to re-stabilize the south.

[S1903M] No binding peace deals were reached. France is the main new opportunity: he says he is striking Germany this spring with A HOL->KIE and A BUR->MUN or A BEL->RUH, and asked me to apply eastern pressure and keep this confidential. I did not promise reckless attacks, but I did signal Germany would not get a free spring in the east. Italy remains cooperative and says A TYR will pressure VIE, A ALB will pressure SER, and fleets will secure ADR/ION; however I did not confirm any exact Russian move into BUD and made clear WAR security comes first, so this is soft coordination only. England offered no real de-escalation after the STP stab; I told him only proof matters and demanded he stay out of SWE/BOT/BAL, with no concessions from me. Turkey explicitly declared he intends to take SEV and offered only a promise-based ceasefire if I yield it; I refused, so assume full Turkish hostility. Germany explicitly said he is attacking WAR again this spring; assume renewed PRU/SIL pressure. Key board-read to remember: Germany, Austria, and Turkey remain the active anti-Russian bloc; England is still opportunistic and dangerous but not yet part of a formal coordinated deal this turn; France and Italy are the only useful counterweights.
Intent: Primary intent is still survival with WAR the top priority. I do not intend to honor any Turkish demand to concede SEV, but in practice I likely cannot save both WAR and SEV; WAR remains more important. I made no binding exact-move promise to France or Italy, only a soft commitment that Germany will not get a free spring and that Austria/GAL will stay under strain if possible. I do not intend any voluntary northern concession to England; if England stays out of SWE/BOT/BAL, fine, but I am trusting only board proof.

[S1903M] Spring 1903 confirmed the board lines clearly. Germany did exactly what he said: PRU-SIL pressure on WAR again, but MOS support kept WAR alive, which was the right priority. Turkey also carried out his threat exactly, taking SEV with ARM supported by RUM and re-entering BLA from ANK; no trust remains there. On the positive side, France fully honored his anti-German plan, taking KIE and MUN, which is the biggest strategic bright spot. I made no promise to honor Germany's request that I not exploit his western crisis; if a safe anti-German move exists, I intend to take it.

Germany clearly pivoted west, moving SIL->MUN and PRU->LVN; his “no attack on WAR” claim was true this turn, but LVN keeps pressure alive, so no trust restored. [S1904M] No binding deals were reached. Austria refused the key proof I demanded, namely vacating GAL; instead he floated anti-Italy/France cooperation and claimed he would show peace by not moving GAL->WAR/UKR this spring, which I did not accept as sufficient. Net takeaway: France and Italy are still the only useful counterweights, but with only A WAR and A MOS left, survival comes first and no one has earned enough trust to justify exposing Warsaw.
Intent: Primary S1904M intent is still WAR-first survival with active defense rather than passive holding. Default plan is to keep Austria from having a free shot from GAL while preserving WAR, most likely with A WAR->GAL and A MOS->WAR. I made no binding order commitments to anyone. I do not intend to honor Germany's request to freeze the east, and I do not intend to join Austria's anti-Italy/France line. I also do not currently intend to fulfill France's riskier anti-German idea via a WAR move toward SIL/PRU, because that would open Warsaw unless Austria proves restraint on the board; only if late evidence makes WAR clearly safe would I consider a stronger anti-German interference move instead.

[S1904M] My WAR-first active defense was correct: A WAR-GAL bounced and, crucially, cut Austria’s support for Turkey’s SEV->UKR move, keeping WAR secure and proving again that passive defense would have been worse. Austria did not give the board-proof restraint I wanted; instead he stayed in GAL and visibly coordinated with Turkey. Turkey executed a strong southern rotation anyway, ending with UKR/SEV/BLA pressure intact and the southern threat still severe. England’s talk of eastern de-escalation was only partially borne out: he made no new direct move against me, but he openly supported Germany back into KIE, showing he is still willing to strengthen my enemies when useful. France failed to carry out the hoped-for anti-German pressure and lost KIE, so western relief weakened. Italy kept fighting but Austria/Turkey gained in the Ionian. No promises were broken by me because I made none.

[F1904M] No binding agreements were made. Austria suddenly claimed Turkey stabbed him and proposed a RU-A truce built around A GAL->UKR with Russian support, but he still refused the only proof that matters: vacating GAL first. Treat this as opportunistic and untrusted. France again pushed for anti-German cooperation and specifically asked for A WAR->SIL to help finish Germany, claiming Italy would keep GAL occupied; I did not agree because GAL is still occupied and WAR cannot be exposed on promises. Germany again asked for an eastern freeze and explicitly said to let Turkey handle the south; I rejected this and noted that only board-proof restraint matters. Italy remained the most cooperative southern partner, urging continued pressure on Austria; I encouraged him to keep Austrian units tied down but gave no exact move commitment. Turkey was fully explicit that he does not intend to ease pressure and even suggested I concede WAR for a temporary reprieve; this was rejected and confirms total hostility. Key board lesson from spring must be remembered: active anti-GAL defense in S1904 cut support and saved WAR, but with both GAL and UKR now adjacent in fall, pure activity may no longer be board-safe if it risks a supported capture of WAR.
Intent: Primary intent for F1904M is still WAR-first survival, now with the strongest board-safe defense as the default. Unless a clearly safe tactical change appears at order entry, plan is A WAR H and A MOS S A WAR to prevent a supported GAL/UKR capture. I made no binding commitments and do not intend to fulfill France's requested A WAR->SIL, Austria's requested support for GAL->UKR, Germany's proposed freeze, or Turkey's demand that I concede WAR. If late board reading shows one of GAL or UKR is clearly neutralized, I can reconsider a more active anti-GAL/anti-German move, but default is full defense of Warsaw.

[F1904M] No binding deals existed, so no promises were broken by me or clearly by anyone else. My WAR-first defense was still correct: MOS support was cut by Turkey’s UKR->MOS, but because neither Austria nor Turkey actually attacked WAR, both of my centers survived.
