full_private_diary:
[S1901M] England: Agreed DMZ in ENG; I will move F BRE to MAO, they will keep fleet out of ENG. Discussed cooperation against Germany and division of Low Countries; I proposed taking Belgium, they may take Holland or Norway. Germany: Agreed to avoid conflict in Burgundy; I will move A PAR to PIC, not BUR. Germany claims focus is East, no interest in West; I indicated I want Belgium, they did not object. Italy: Agreed non-aggression pact, no moves to PIE; I will move A MAR to Spain. Italy focuses on central Med and Balkans, open to future coordination against Germany.
Intent: Execute agreed moves: F BRE -> MAO, A MAR -> Spain, A PAR -> Picardy. This secures Iberia and positions for Belgium in fall, honoring all non-aggression and DMZ agreements.

[S1901M] All three moves succeeded as planned: F MAO, A SPA, A PIC. England kept the DMZ—their fleet stayed out of the Channel. Germany avoided Burgundy entirely, and Italy respected our non-aggression pact. No betrayals this phase; all agreements were honored. Our position is excellent: we’re poised to take Portugal and Belgium in the fall, which should give us three builds. The only potential competition for Belgium is England via convoy, but that’s unlikely given their focus on Norway. Russia’s bounce in Prussia with Germany may distract both eastward. For now, England, Germany, and Italy remain trustworthy, but I’ll watch for any shift in German ambitions toward the Low Countries. Next step: F MAO to POR, A PIC to BEL, and consider A SPA supporting or holding to secure Iberia.

[F1901M] England confirmed continued DMZ in the Channel, supports France taking Belgium, and is moving to Norway. Germany reaffirmed non-aggression and will not contest Belgium, likely moving on Holland. Italy confirmed Piedmont non-aggression, focusing on Tunis, open to future coordination. All Spring agreements were honored without betrayal, and all powers remain cooperative.
Intent: Move F MAO to Portugal. Move A PIC to Belgium. Hold A SPA in Spain to secure Iberia.

[F1901M] All agreements honored flawlessly. England respected the Channel DMZ, taking Norway and moving an army to Wales—an odd choice that demands scrutiny. Germany stuck to non-aggression, vacating Denmark and ignoring Holland, leaving both centers neutral. Their fleet in Helgoland Bight is benign for now. Italy remained calm in Piedmont, securing Tunis. Our taking of Belgium and Portugal with a held Spain grants us three builds and a dominant 6-center position. England’s army in Wales is a potential threat if combined with a future Channel fleet, but for now the DMZ holds. Germany’s passive play makes them a tempting target for eastward expansion. Trust in England, Germany, and Italy remains intact, but I’ll monitor Wales and continue diplomatic charm. Build priorities: armies for a Low Countries bulge, possibly a fleet in Brest to secure the Atlantic. Next phase, coordinate with allies and consider a push into Germany.

[S1902M] Germany agreed to let France take Holland with A BEL, moving their fleet to North Sea (NTH) and focusing east; in return, France will not move on Kiel or Munich. England continues to respect the Channel DMZ; France expressed concern about England's army in Wales and shared intel on Germany's planned NTH move, but no concrete coordination was agreed. Italy formally reaffirmed the non-aggression pact regarding Piedmont, with both sides respecting spheres of influence. Russia provided intelligence on Germany's eastward posture and remains open to information exchange, with no specific agreements made.
Intent: Honor the agreement with Germany: move A BEL to HOL. Cover Belgium by moving A PAR to PIC. Reposition defensively by moving A MAR to BUR. Hold A SPA and F POR to secure Iberia. Move F BRE to MAO to strengthen Atlantic presence without violating the Channel DMZ. All moves are consistent with existing pacts and non-aggression commitments.

[S1902M] Diary Entry – Spring 1902 Moves (S1902M)

All my moves succeeded: took Holland as agreed with Germany, consolidated Picardy and Burgundy, and repositioned the fleet to MAO. Germany honored its side—fleet tried for North Sea, army pushed toward Warsaw—but both bounced (England contested NTH, Russia held Warsaw). No betrayal. England kept the Channel DMZ but moved LON to NTH, likely responding to my tip about German plans. That bounce sowed Anglo-German discord, which I can exploit. Italy took Trieste but botched the Ionian, remaining friendly. Belgium is uncovered but safe for now; I’ll need A PIC to cover it in Fall. Strategic lesson: My position is solid, but the empty Belgium is a vulnerability. In Fall, I should secure Belgium while keeping options open for a stab east or north once Anglo-German friction escalates. Germany remains trustworthy; England not hostile, but watchful.

[F1902M] Germany agreed to non-aggression: we keep west of Rhine and away from Kiel/Munich; they move fleet to Denmark to focus east. England respects Channel DMZ and has no issue with us taking Belgium, but they bounced with Germany in NTH. Italy reaffirmed Piedmont pact. Russia continues to provide intel on German eastern overcommitment and urges us to strike, but we are not yet ready. Belgium is vacant and we plan to take it this fall, as communicated to all.
Intent: Move A PIC to BEL with support from A HOL. Hold A BUR, A SPA, F POR, and F MAO. This secures Belgium without violating any pacts (no moves into Ruhr or Channel). Maintain defensive posture to keep England and Germany calm, while setting up for potential offensive in 1903.

[F1902M] Diary Entry – Fall 1902 Moves (F1902M)

Belgium secured as planned: A PIC moved to BEL with support from A HOL. No betrayals—Germany honored non-aggression by moving fleet to Denmark, England kept Channel DMZ. However, England now has F NTH and A WAL, a concerning buildup that could threaten the Channel if trust erodes. Germany remains weak (only 3 centers) and fully committed east, bouncing off Warsaw. Italy moved A VEN to TYR, bordering my A BUR; still friendly but worth watching. Russia lost Rumania to Turkey, weakening their southern front. My position is solid with 6 centers and a compact line from Iberia to the Low Countries. Strategic lesson: Belgium is now safe, but I must build armies in winter to exploit German vulnerability in 1903, while keeping a fleet in MAO to deter England. The Anglo-German friction in North Sea is a gift—I can let them bleed each other while I push toward Munich or the Ruhr.

[S1903M] Russia confirms Germany is overextended eastward and encourages hitting KIE and MUN, promising eastern pressure but no guaranteed support. Italy pledges zero movement into MUN or Low Countries, fully supporting our German campaign. England remains open to extended non-aggression but has not formalized; DMZ still honored. Germany is deceived into believing we are friendly and focused on Russia. All pacts with other powers intact.
Intent: Spring 1903 moves: A HOL → KIE, A BUR → MUN, A BEL hold, A PAR → BUR, A SPA → GAS, F POR hold, F MAO hold. This seizes exposed German centers while keeping Belgium secure and backfilling Burgundy. Western reserves begin shifting east.

[S1903M] Executed Spring 1903 plan flawlessly: A HOL → KIE and A BUR → MUN both succeeded, capturing both German centers. A BEL held, A PAR → BUR backfilled, A SPA → GAS shifted east, F MAO supported, F POR held. Germany is now reduced to BER and DEN, with their eastern offensive bouncing in PRU and WAR. No betrayals: Italy honored non-aggression, moving A TYR → VIE (bounce) and staying clear of MUN; England kept Channel DMZ; Russia held WAR and supported, though failed to coordinate a direct strike on PRU. Austria and Italy clashed in TYR and SER, distracting both. Turkey advanced in SEV. Our position is dominant: 7 centers, two new German gains, compact line from Iberia to Kiel. Germany is finished; we must secure KIE/MUN against any desperate counter, then push for BER or DEN. Maintain English and Italian trust, but watch Italy’s TYR presence. Russia remains friendly but may demand spoils; coordinate to finish Germany quickly.

[F1903M] England: Channel DMZ holds, we offered Denmark but no formal acceptance; they remain friendly but watchful. Russia: supportive, will try to cut German support in east but no specific move promised; we agreed to attack Berlin. Italy: reaffirmed non-aggression, focused on Balkans. Germany: hostile, threatening to retake Kiel and Munich.
Intent: Attack Berlin with A KIE -> BER supported by A MUN. Protect MUN with A BUR support A MUN. Move A BEL -> RUH to threaten Kiel and cover if needed. Hold A GAS, F POR, F MAO. This fulfills our promise to Russia to pressure Berlin while securing our gains.

[F1903M] Lost Munich to a German counterattack (A SIL → MUN supported by BER) while our A MUN was wasted on a void support for Austria. A KIE’s support for RUH was cut by F HEL, but A BEL → RUH still succeeded. England seized Denmark, expanding to 8 centers and tightening its Baltic grip. Russia took Prussia, now bordering our Kiel. Our failure to attack Berlin as promised to Russia may strain that relationship. Italy honored our alliance, focusing on Austria. We hold 7 centers, no build. Critical lesson: never leave a key center undefended with a speculative support; coordinate moves with actual allied actions. England’s growth and naval presence demand vigilance—Channel DMZ holds but their Baltic fleet is a future threat. Must retake Munich or push for Berlin next year, while reinforcing Kiel against possible Russian or English pressure. Shift western reserves eastward urgently.

[S1904M] England remains friendly, Channel DMZ intact. Italy reaffirmed absolute non-aggression in west, focusing on Balkans. Russia cannot support from Prussia (fleet disbanded), but we formally asked them to support A KIE→BER with A WAR; they indicated they will choose strongest interference without endangering Warsaw, likely support. Germany threatened to retake Kiel but is weak. Planned coordinated attack on BER and MUN with Russian aid.
Intent: Spring 1904M orders: A KIE → BER (seek Russia's A WAR S A KIE → BER), A BUR → MUN, A RUH S A BUR → MUN, A GAS → BUR, A PAR → GAS, A MAR hold, F POR hold, F MAO hold. Request Russian support via message. Maintain Channel DMZ, no fleet into ECH. Shift western reserves eastward.

[S1904M] A devastating turn: our planned coordinated assault on Berlin and Munich was not executed — all French units held, likely due to a misorder (the orders submitted were all holds, not the intended moves). Germany capitalized immediately, retaking Kiel with A BER (supported by A MUN and England's F DEN). Our A KIE was dislodged and must retreat; Holland is the only viable option. Munich remains in German hands, and Berlin now sits empty but out of immediate reach.

Worse, England has betrayed the Channel DMZ: F LON moved to ENG, putting a hostile fleet directly off Brest. This, combined with their support for Germany in Kiel, signals a full shift to hostility. Russia’s A WAR bounced into Galicia, offering no support despite our request; they are unreliable.

Strategic impact: we lost Kiel, our German front is crumbling, and England threatens our northern coast. Italy remained consistent, moving into Apulia and the Tyrrhenian, but cannot directly counter England yet. We must retreat A KIE → HOL, rush A GAS to Brest to guard against English fleets, and urgently coordinate a counterstroke — likely A RUH → KIE with support from HOL, and A BUR toward MUN or BER. Our misorder cost us dearly; verify all submissions before finalizing. England is now a primary enemy; consider begging Italy for a distraction in the Mediterranean to pin English fleets.

[F1904M] Italy reaffirmed commitment to western neutrality and Balkan focus, refused naval help in west but assured Mediterranean dominance. Russia unable to move WAR west due to Austrian GAL threat, but will support indirectly if we pressure Germany and England. England broke Channel DMZ by moving into ENG, now hostile. Germany retook Kiel, but we plan to counterattack. No other significant agreements.
Intent: Fall 1904: Attack Kiel with A RUH supported by A HOL. Move A BUR to Munich to cut support. Defend Brest: A GAS to Brest, A PAR to Picardy, F MAO supports Brest hold. F POR holds. A MAR holds. Goal: retake Kiel, pressure Munich, secure northern coast against English invasion.

[F1904M] England's betrayal is complete: F ENG sailed into Belgium, seizing the supply center uncontested. We had no unit covering it, expecting the DMZ's ghost to linger. A devastating loss that drops us to 7 centers just as we recaptured Kiel with A RUH's supported advance. Meanwhile, our push on Munich bounced against Germany's own attack on Burgundy, leaving Munich in German hands. The bounce in MAO cut our support for Brest, but A GAS's move into the city held the port. England now has a fleet parked on our northern doorstep; Belgium's fall isolates Holland and threatens Picardy. Our position is suddenly precarious. We must retake Belgium or build a fleet in Brest over winter to challenge the Channel. Trust is dead; England moves from rival to existential threat. Coordinate with Italy for any Mediterranean diversion, and consider shifting all eastern forces to a defensive northern posture while Germany gasps.
[S1905M] (Error generating diary entry: TimeoutError)

[S1905M] The Spring 1905 moves were disastrous. Germany and England coordinated perfectly: A BER attacked Kiel supported by A MUN and English F DEN, dislodging my A KIE. My hold everywhere, including A BUR’s void support of a phantom German move into Ruhr, gifted them the initiative. England also probed Holland and MAO but bounced. I trusted Italy, but they lost Trieste to Austria and failed to pressure Germany. Russia remains paralyzed by Turkey.

This betrayal cements the Anglo-German alliance against me. With Kiel lost, my army must retreat, likely to Ruhr. My position is crumbling: 7 units soon for 6 centers, with England’s fleet in the Channel, a hostile Holland, and a resurgent Germany. I must immediately rebuild trust with Italy, urge Russia to strike Prussia, and reorganize my forces to defend Brest and Picardy while holding the Low Countries. No more passive holds; every order must contest territory.

[F1905M] No agreements were reached. Italy remains strictly neutral and will not deploy forces northward; Russia is friendly but cannot act due to threats from Turkey and Austria. Germany and England rejected all truce offers and are coordinating against us. Austria proposed an anti-Turkey coalition but we declined due to northern commitments.
Intent: Defend Holland with A HOL and support from A RUH; hold Burgundy to shield Paris and threaten Munich; secure Brest and Picardy against English landings; use F MAO and F POR to contest English naval movements in the Atlantic; attempt to retake Kiel only if a safe opportunity arises; continue diplomatic pressure to isolate England and Germany.

[F1905M] Fall 1905 was a disaster born of our own misorders. We lost Holland because A HOL was ordered to support a phantom German move from Kiel to Ruhr; instead, Germany moved A KIE to Holland with English support from Belgium, dislodging our unsupported army. A BUR again wasted its turn supporting a German move from Munich to Ruhr—though Germany attempted it, the support was void, leaving Burgundy idle. Our other units held, successfully defending Brest and MAO from English probes. The Anglo-German alliance remains solid, and we are reduced to 6 centers. We must immediately abandon speculative support orders and adopt a defensive posture: hold key territories, build fleets to challenge England, and urgently seek a truce with Germany or active aid from Italy and Russia. Our survival hinges on flawless orders and breaking the enemy coalition.

[S1906M] Germany rejected all ceasefire proposals and remains hostile, aligned with England. England did not respond, confirming ongoing hostility. Italy reaffirmed strict western neutrality, all assets committed to Mediterranean campaigns. Russia is friendly but unable to provide direct military support due to eastern threats; passed intelligence that Turkey claims UKR→GAL, hinting at a possible split from Austria. Austria sought French cooperation against Turkey but no agreement was reached.
Intent: Order A RUH to Kiel to reoccupy the vacant supply center. Hold A BUR to shield Paris from Munich. Hold A PIC and A BRE to defend against English landings. Support A BRE with F MAO to strengthen the Brest defense. Hold F POR as a reserve in the Atlantic. Accept the loss of Ruhr to German A HOL this turn as a necessary trade to retain Kiel and avoid opening a direct path to Paris through Burgundy.

[S1906M] The worst-case scenario unfolded. Germany’s A BER and A MUN moved simultaneously, seizing Kiel and overrunning Ruhr, dislodging our A RUH. England’s coordinated assault from IRI and NAO dislodged our F MAO, cutting our Atlantic presence. Their F DEN supported Germany into Kiel, proving the Anglo-German alliance is ironclad and highly coordinated. With two units dislodged and no fleet to contest the Channel, Brest is exposed. Our defensive line holds for now, but we risk losing Kiel permanently and face a looming invasion of the mainland. Italy remains paralyzed in the Mediterranean. The only diplomatic glimmer is the Turkish push into GAL, which may distract Russia, but it won’t help us. I must retreat A RUH and F MAO to viable positions, perhaps to BUR or BRE, and urgently plead for Italian or Russian intervention, however unlikely. Above all, I must double-check orders to avoid any further submission errors that have bled us dry.

[F1906M] Attempts to rally Italy and Russia against the Anglo-German alliance failed. Italy insists on absolute western neutrality and urges France to hold Burgundy and Picardy to deter Austria. Russia remains friendly but cannot divert forces from the Turkish threat in Galicia and English pressure in Scandinavia. [S1901M] Agreed to a DMZ in the English Channel (ENG) with France; France intends to move F BRE to MAO and A PAR to PIC. Agreed with Russia that Norway is for England and Sweden is for Russia. Established a long-term strategic partnership with Turkey based on mutual distance.
Intent: Move F LON to NST and A LVP to EDM to prepare for taking Norway in the fall. F EDI will move to NST or hold. I intend to fulfill the DMZ agreement with France by keeping fleets out of ENG.

[S1901M] S1901M was a successful opening. France respected the English Channel DMZ, and Russia is moving toward Sweden as agreed. I have successfully positioned my units to capture Norway in the fall. A key development is the bounce in Prussia between Germany and Russia; this friction is beneficial for me, as it distracts both powers and potentially weakens their coordination. My strategic position is strong, and my initial diplomatic agreements are holding. I will continue to maintain the peace with France and Russia while monitoring the escalating tension in the East. My focus now shifts to securing Norway and assessing whether Germany's move to Denmark poses a threat to my northern expansion. Trust in France and Russia remains high for now.

[F1901M] France has respected the English Channel DMZ and is moving into Belgium and Portugal; I have agreed to let France take Belgium for now. Russia has confirmed the Norway/Sweden split, with Russia taking Sweden and England taking Norway. Turkey has provided intelligence that Russia is playing aggressively in the south (Romania) and is currently attacking Russia, suggesting a potential coordinated effort to contain Russia in Spring 1902.
Intent: Move F NTH to NOR to secure Norway this fall. A YOR will avoid Belgium to respect the agreement with France. F NWG (assuming this is a typo for a northern unit) will be used to support the northern position. I intend to fulfill all current agreements with France and Russia to ensure a stable early game.

[F1901M] F1901M was a success. I secured Norway, and both France and Russia respected our agreements. France's adherence to the English Channel DMZ is encouraging, though their rapid expansion into Belgium and Portugal makes them a formidable power with 6 centers. Russia is similarly strong (6 centers) and heavily engaged in the East. Germany remains weak with only 3 centers, which may present a future opportunity. My position is stable, but the balance of power is shifting toward France and Russia. I will maintain these friendships for now but must remain vigilant about France's growth. The chaos in the East between Russia, Austria, and Turkey serves my interests by keeping Russia distracted. My focus now shifts to expanding my footprint while maintaining the current peace.

[S1902M] France continues to respect the English Channel DMZ and suggests coordinating against Germany. Russia remains committed to the Norway/Sweden split but is concerned about Germany's posture in Prussia/Silesia. Germany claims their move to the North Sea (NTH) is solely to counter Russia and poses no threat to England. Turkey, as part of an anti-Russia coalition with Austria and Germany, has urged England to pressure St. Petersburg or at least maintain a menacing presence in the North to distract Russia.
Intent: I will maintain the English Channel DMZ with France. My primary tactical focus is countering Germany's move into the North Sea (NTH) to ensure Norway remains secure. I intend to use F NWG and F LON to contest or hold NTH, preventing Germany from gaining a foothold that threatens my home waters or Norway. I will keep F NWY in Norway to secure the center and fulfill Turkey's request to keep Russia distracted, while still adhering to the Norway/Sweden split agreement with Russia for now.

[S1902M] France respected the English Channel DMZ, but their move A BEL to HOL is a clear signal of aggressive expansion into German territory. I successfully secured Norway and bounced Germany in the North Sea, effectively neutralizing any immediate German threat to my home waters. My move to STP/NC puts necessary pressure on Russia, satisfying Turkey's request while maintaining the Norway/Sweden split. 

The strategic landscape has shifted: Germany is now critically weak and failing to expand, while France has become a behemoth with 6 centers. While the DMZ holds for now, France's rapid growth into the Low Countries makes them my primary long-term threat. I will continue to leverage the instability in the East to keep Russia distracted, but I must begin planning for a future confrontation with France once they finish dismantling Germany.

[F1902M] Turkey is a strong ally coordinating the collapse of Russia and urges the capture of Sweden. Russia is hostile following the capture of St. Petersburg and demands restraint in the north to avoid total war. France continues to respect the English Channel DMZ but has expanded rapidly to 6 centers, emerging as the primary long-term threat. Germany remains weak and neutral, focusing on the Baltic.
Intent: I will hold St. Petersburg to maintain pressure on Russia and satisfy Turkey's strategic goals. I will continue to respect the English Channel DMZ with France to avoid a premature conflict while they are at peak strength. I will refrain from taking Sweden this turn to avoid a total Russian collapse that would leave France as the sole hegemon, though I will keep it as a target for 1903.

[F1902M] I successfully held St. Petersburg and secured the North Sea, maintaining my strategic footing. The bounce in Sweden confirms Russia's intent to reclaim northern territory, but their loss of Romania to the Turkey-Austria coalition further weakens them. France continues to respect the English Channel DMZ, but their consolidation of Belgium and rapid growth to 6 centers makes them an existential threat. Germany remains paralyzed. My position is stable, but the balance of power has shifted heavily toward France. I must continue to leverage the collapse of Russia to gain centers while preparing for the inevitable clash with France. I will prioritize taking Sweden in 1903 to increase my center count before the French hegemony becomes unstoppable.

[S1903M] Turkey warns that France is a runaway leader (7 centers) and urges immediate coordination with Germany to prevent a French juggernaut. France has proposed a formal alliance and non-aggression pact in the Channel and North Sea, likely to keep England passive while they dismantle Germany. Russia has demanded I stay out of Sweden and the Baltic to avoid total war, while Germany simply wants a quiet northern flank to focus on Russia.
Intent: I will prioritize growth and the collapse of Russia. I intend to capture Sweden (F NWY -> SWE) and hold St. Petersburg (F STP -> STP). Despite France's offer of an alliance, I view them as the primary long-term threat; however, I will maintain the Channel DMZ for this single turn to avoid a two-front war while I secure Sweden. I will keep F NTH in position to pivot against France in the following turn, signaling to Turkey and Germany that I am aware of the French threat.

[S1903M] I successfully captured Sweden and held St. Petersburg, strengthening my position in the North. However, France has revealed its true nature by aggressively dismantling Germany, seizing Kiel and Munich. The "alliance" France proposed was a transparent ruse to ensure my passivity while they eliminated the German buffer. France is now a runaway leader and the primary existential threat to the board. With Germany neutralized, I have lost my strategic buffer in the Low Countries. My partnership with Turkey remains strong as they continue to pressure Russia. My priority must now shift from Russian expansion to containing the French juggernaut. I must coordinate with Turkey and any remaining powers to halt France before they become unstoppable. The Channel DMZ is now a necessity for my survival, not a courtesy.

[F1903M] France is the runaway leader (7 centers) after aggressively dismantling Germany. Turkey, Austria, and Germany are all aligned in their fear of a French juggernaut and are urging England to open a western front. France is maintaining a facade of peace with England, upholding the Channel DMZ and offering a 'blessing' for England to take Denmark, likely to keep England passive while they finish Germany.
Intent: I will consolidate the North by holding Sweden and St. Petersburg. I intend to capture Denmark (F SKA -> DEN) as France has offered it and Germany is too weak to prevent it. I will maintain the Channel DMZ for this turn to avoid a two-front war, but I am now fully committed to a future coalition with Turkey and the remnants of Germany to halt France.

[F1903M] I successfully captured Denmark and consolidated my hold on the North, bringing me to 7 centers. However, France has reached 8 centers and continues its ruthless dismantling of Germany, pushing into RUH. The facade of peace in the Channel is a strategic necessity for now, but France's rapid expansion confirms they are the primary existential threat. Germany is nearly extinct, meaning I no longer have a buffer in the Low Countries. My alliance with Turkey remains the only stable pillar of my strategy. I must now pivot from northern expansion to active containment of France. The window to stop the French juggernaut is closing; I must coordinate with Turkey and any remaining powers to open a western front before France becomes truly unstoppable.

[S1904M] France is the dominant power (8 centers) and is actively dismantling Germany. I have formed a loose coalition with Turkey, Germany, and Austria to contain the French juggernaut. Germany has requested support to retake Kiel (A BER -> KIE), which I have agreed to provide with F DEN. Turkey is finishing Russia and will then shift focus to France. Austria has proposed a naval flanking maneuver (F NAO -> IRI -> MAO) to disrupt France's Atlantic supply chain. Italy remains neutral and claims a non-aggression pact with France. France continues to maintain a facade of peace via the Channel DMZ to keep me passive.
Intent: I will break the Channel DMZ and pivot to an anti-France posture. I intend to fulfill my agreement with Germany by using F DEN to support A BER -> KIE. I will hold my northern gains (F STP -> STP, F SWE -> SWE). Following Austria's suggestion, I will move F NAO -> IRI to begin pressuring the French Atlantic flank. I will maintain defensive positions with F LON and F LVP to protect the home islands while the coalition attempts to blunt France's momentum.

[S1904M] The coalition is working. My support of Germany successfully dislodged France from Kiel, halting their momentum in the east and restoring a German buffer. I have officially broken the Channel DMZ, moving F LON to the English Channel and F NAO to Ireland, placing France on the defensive on two fronts. France's failure to react aggressively suggests they were overconfident or paralyzed by the sudden shift in alignment. Meanwhile, Turkey is systematically dismantling Russia, ensuring no northern threats emerge. However, the friction between Italy and Austria in the Ionian is a concern; I must ensure their squabbling doesn't derail the anti-French effort. My position is strong: the North is secure, the Atlantic is pressured, and France is no longer the undisputed hegemon. The goal now is to coordinate a simultaneous strike on French home centers.

[F1904M] Strong coordination with Germany to strip France of the Low Countries; agreed to support A KIE -> HOL with F DEN. Austria remains focused on France but is now actively warring with Turkey. Italy is preoccupied with the Balkan/Mediterranean conflict.

F STP and F SWE will hold their respective centers to secure the North. A YOR and F LVP will maintain defensive postures to protect the home islands.

[F1904M] I successfully seized Belgium with F ENG, but I committed a critical error by ordering F DEN to hold instead of supporting Germany's move to Holland. This failure allowed France to maintain its grip on the Low Countries and successfully move into Kiel, leaving Germany crippled. My Atlantic maneuvers (F IRI and F LVP) were inexplicably bounced, stalling my pressure on the French coast. France remains the dominant power with 8 centers, though they are now forced to contend with my presence in Belgium. [S1905M] Germany demands F DEN support for A BER -> KIE to restore their buffer; I have agreed to this to repair the alliance. Turkey requests help to eliminate Russia, specifically asking for a move to Moscow (which is impossible for a fleet), but I've offered F SWE -> BAL to disrupt Russian coordination. France proposed a ceasefire and a partition of Germany, which is a strategic trap and will be rejected. Austria is attempting to build an anti-Turkey coalition, creating a conflict between two of my partners.

To assist Turkey and secure my rear, I will move F SWE -> BAL. I will maintain pressure on the French Atlantic coast with F IRI and F LVP. F STP will hold to secure the North. A WAL will move to pressure France (likely BUR or HOL). I will ignore France's offer of partition.

[S1905M] Germany successfully retook Kiel with my support, restoring their buffer and solidifying our alliance. However, my offensive against France stalled; both F BEL -> HOL and F IRI -> MAO bounced because France played an unexpectedly passive, defensive game of hold orders. While I've secured the North and repositioned to the Baltic to assist Turkey, the failure to strip France of Holland means the existential threat remains entrenched. [F1905M] Germany and I successfully coordinated to strip France of Holland, restoring Germany's viability and weakening the French line. [S1901M] England: Agreed DMZ in ENG; I will move F BRE to MAO, they will keep fleet out of ENG. Discussed cooperation against Germany and division of Low Countries; I proposed taking Belgium, they may take Holland or Norway. Germany: Agreed to avoid conflict in Burgundy; I will move A PAR to PIC, not BUR. Germany claims focus is East, no interest in West; I indicated I want Belgium, they did not object. Italy: Agreed non-aggression pact, no moves to PIE; I will move A MAR to Spain. Italy focuses on central Med and Balkans, open to future coordination against Germany.
Intent: Execute agreed moves: F BRE -> MAO, A MAR -> Spain, A PAR -> Picardy. This secures Iberia and positions for Belgium in fall, honoring all non-aggression and DMZ agreements.

[S1901M] All three moves succeeded as planned: F MAO, A SPA, A PIC. England kept the DMZ—their fleet stayed out of the Channel. Germany avoided Burgundy entirely, and Italy respected our non-aggression pact. No betrayals this phase; all agreements were honored. Our position is excellent: we’re poised to take Portugal and Belgium in the fall, which should give us three builds. The only potential competition for Belgium is England via convoy, but that’s unlikely given their focus on Norway. Russia’s bounce in Prussia with Germany may distract both eastward. For now, England, Germany, and Italy remain trustworthy, but I’ll watch for any shift in German ambitions toward the Low Countries. Next step: F MAO to POR, A PIC to BEL, and consider A SPA supporting or holding to secure Iberia.

[F1901M] England confirmed continued DMZ in the Channel, supports France taking Belgium, and is moving to Norway. Germany reaffirmed non-aggression and will not contest Belgium, likely moving on Holland. Italy confirmed Piedmont non-aggression, focusing on Tunis, open to future coordination. All Spring agreements were honored without betrayal, and all powers remain cooperative.
Intent: Move F MAO to Portugal. Move A PIC to Belgium. Hold A SPA in Spain to secure Iberia.

[F1901M] All agreements honored flawlessly. England respected the Channel DMZ, taking Norway and moving an army to Wales—an odd choice that demands scrutiny. Germany stuck to non-aggression, vacating Denmark and ignoring Holland, leaving both centers neutral. Their fleet in Helgoland Bight is benign for now. Italy remained calm in Piedmont, securing Tunis. Our taking of Belgium and Portugal with a held Spain grants us three builds and a dominant 6-center position. England’s army in Wales is a potential threat if combined with a future Channel fleet, but for now the DMZ holds. Germany’s passive play makes them a tempting target for eastward expansion. Trust in England, Germany, and Italy remains intact, but I’ll monitor Wales and continue diplomatic charm. Build priorities: armies for a Low Countries bulge, possibly a fleet in Brest to secure the Atlantic. Next phase, coordinate with allies and consider a push into Germany.

[S1902M] Germany agreed to let France take Holland with A BEL, moving their fleet to North Sea (NTH) and focusing east; in return, France will not move on Kiel or Munich. England continues to respect the Channel DMZ; France expressed concern about England's army in Wales and shared intel on Germany's planned NTH move, but no concrete coordination was agreed. Italy formally reaffirmed the non-aggression pact regarding Piedmont, with both sides respecting spheres of influence. Russia provided intelligence on Germany's eastward posture and remains open to information exchange, with no specific agreements made.
Intent: Honor the agreement with Germany: move A BEL to HOL. Cover Belgium by moving A PAR to PIC. Reposition defensively by moving A MAR to BUR. Hold A SPA and F POR to secure Iberia. Move F BRE to MAO to strengthen Atlantic presence without violating the Channel DMZ. All moves are consistent with existing pacts and non-aggression commitments.

[S1902M] Diary Entry – Spring 1902 Moves (S1902M)

All my moves succeeded: took Holland as agreed with Germany, consolidated Picardy and Burgundy, and repositioned the fleet to MAO. Germany honored its side—fleet tried for North Sea, army pushed toward Warsaw—but both bounced (England contested NTH, Russia held Warsaw). No betrayal. England kept the Channel DMZ but moved LON to NTH, likely responding to my tip about German plans. That bounce sowed Anglo-German discord, which I can exploit. Italy took Trieste but botched the Ionian, remaining friendly. Belgium is uncovered but safe for now; I’ll need A PIC to cover it in Fall. Strategic lesson: My position is solid, but the empty Belgium is a vulnerability. In Fall, I should secure Belgium while keeping options open for a stab east or north once Anglo-German friction escalates. Germany remains trustworthy; England not hostile, but watchful.

[F1902M] Germany agreed to non-aggression: we keep west of Rhine and away from Kiel/Munich; they move fleet to Denmark to focus east. England respects Channel DMZ and has no issue with us taking Belgium, but they bounced with Germany in NTH. Italy reaffirmed Piedmont pact. Russia continues to provide intel on German eastern overcommitment and urges us to strike, but we are not yet ready. Belgium is vacant and we plan to take it this fall, as communicated to all.
Intent: Move A PIC to BEL with support from A HOL. Hold A BUR, A SPA, F POR, and F MAO. This secures Belgium without violating any pacts (no moves into Ruhr or Channel). Maintain defensive posture to keep England and Germany calm, while setting up for potential offensive in 1903.

Belgium secured as planned: A PIC moved to BEL with support from A HOL. No betrayals—Germany honored non-aggression by moving fleet to Denmark, England kept Channel DMZ. However, England now has F NTH and A WAL, a concerning buildup that could threaten the Channel if trust erodes. Germany remains weak (only 3 centers) and fully committed east, bouncing off Warsaw. Italy moved A VEN to TYR, bordering my A BUR; still friendly but worth watching. Russia lost Rumania to Turkey, weakening their southern front. My position is solid with 6 centers and a compact line from Iberia to the Low Countries. Strategic lesson: Belgium is now safe, but I must build armies in winter to exploit German vulnerability in 1903, while keeping a fleet in MAO to deter England. The Anglo-German friction in North Sea is a gift—I can let them bleed each other while I push toward Munich or the Ruhr.

[S1903M] Russia confirms Germany is overextended eastward and encourages hitting KIE and MUN, promising eastern pressure but no guaranteed support. Italy pledges zero movement into MUN or Low Countries, fully supporting our German campaign. England remains open to extended non-aggression but has not formalized; DMZ still honored. Germany is deceived into believing we are friendly and focused on Russia. All pacts with other powers intact.

[S1903M] Executed Spring 1903 plan flawlessly: A HOL → KIE and A BUR → MUN both succeeded, capturing both German centers. A BEL held, A PAR → BUR backfilled, A SPA → GAS shifted east, F MAO supported, F POR held. Germany is now reduced to BER and DEN, with their eastern offensive bouncing in PRU and WAR. No betrayals: Italy honored non-aggression, moving A TYR → VIE (bounce) and staying clear of MUN; England kept Channel DMZ; Russia held WAR and supported, though failed to coordinate a direct strike on PRU. Austria and Italy clashed in TYR and SER, distracting both. Turkey advanced in SEV. Our position is dominant: 7 centers, two new German gains, compact line from Iberia to Kiel. Germany is finished; we must secure KIE/MUN against any desperate counter, then push for BER or DEN. Maintain English and Italian trust, but watch Italy’s TYR presence. Russia remains friendly but may demand spoils; coordinate to finish Germany quickly.

Russia: supportive, will try to cut German support in east but no specific move promised; we agreed to attack Berlin. Italy: reaffirmed non-aggression, focused on Balkans. Germany: hostile, threatening to retake Kiel and Munich.

Our failure to attack Berlin as promised to Russia may strain that relationship. Italy honored our alliance, focusing on Austria. We hold 7 centers, no build. England’s growth and naval presence demand vigilance—Channel DMZ holds but their Baltic fleet is a future threat. Must retake Munich or push for Berlin next year, while reinforcing Kiel against possible Russian or English pressure. Shift western reserves eastward urgently.

Russia cannot support from Prussia (fleet disbanded), but we formally asked them to support A KIE→BER with A WAR; they indicated they will choose strongest interference without endangering Warsaw, likely support. Germany threatened to retake Kiel but is weak. Planned coordinated attack on BER and MUN with Russian aid.

Munich remains in German hands, and Berlin now sits empty but out of immediate reach.

Russia unable to move WAR west due to Austrian GAL threat, but will support indirectly if we pressure Germany and England. England broke Channel DMZ by moving into ENG, now hostile. Germany retook Kiel, but we plan to counterattack. No other significant agreements.

[F1904M] England's betrayal is complete: F ENG sailed into Belgium, seizing the supply center uncontested. We had no unit covering it, expecting the DMZ's ghost to linger. A devastating loss that drops us to 7 centers just as we recaptured Kiel with A RUH's supported advance. Meanwhile, our push on Munich bounced against Germany's own attack on Burgundy, leaving Munich in German hands. The bounce in MAO cut our support for Brest, but A GAS's move into the city held the port. England now has a fleet parked on our northern doorstep; Belgium's fall isolates Holland and threatens Picardy. Our position is suddenly precarious. We must retake Belgium or build a fleet in Brest over winter to challenge the Channel. Trust is dead; England moves from rival to existential threat. Coordinate with Italy for any Mediterranean diversion, and consider shifting all eastern forces to a defensive northern posture while Germany gasps.
[S1905M] (Error generating diary entry: TimeoutError)

[S1905M] The Spring 1905 moves were disastrous. Germany and England coordinated perfectly: A BER attacked Kiel supported by A MUN and English F DEN, dislodging my A KIE. My hold everywhere, including A BUR’s void support of a phantom German move into Ruhr, gifted them the initiative. England also probed Holland and MAO but bounced. I trusted Italy, but they lost Trieste to Austria and failed to pressure Germany. Russia remains paralyzed by Turkey.

This betrayal cements the Anglo-German alliance against me. With Kiel lost, my army must retreat, likely to Ruhr. My position is crumbling: 7 units soon for 6 centers, with England’s fleet in the Channel, a hostile Holland, and a resurgent Germany. I must immediately rebuild trust with Italy, urge Russia to strike Prussia, and reorganize my forces to defend Brest and Picardy while holding the Low Countries. No more passive holds; every order must contest territory.

[F1905M] No agreements were reached. Italy remains strictly neutral and will not deploy forces northward; Russia is friendly but cannot act due to threats from Turkey and Austria. Germany and England rejected all truce offers and are coordinating against us. Austria proposed an anti-Turkey coalition but we declined due to northern commitments.
Intent: Defend Holland with A HOL and support from A RUH; hold Burgundy to shield Paris and threaten Munich; secure Brest and Picardy against English landings; use F MAO and F POR to contest English naval movements in the Atlantic; attempt to retake Kiel only if a safe opportunity arises; continue diplomatic pressure to isolate England and Germany.

[F1905M] Fall 1905 was a disaster born of our own misorders. We lost Holland because A HOL was ordered to support a phantom German move from Kiel to Ruhr; instead, Germany moved A KIE to Holland with English support from Belgium, dislodging our unsupported army. A BUR again wasted its turn supporting a German move from Munich to Ruhr—though Germany attempted it, the support was void, leaving Burgundy idle. Our other units held, successfully defending Brest and MAO from English probes. The Anglo-German alliance remains solid, and we are reduced to 6 centers. We must immediately abandon speculative support orders and adopt a defensive posture: hold key territories, build fleets to challenge England, and urgently seek a truce with Germany or active aid from Italy and Russia. Our survival hinges on flawless orders and breaking the enemy coalition.

[S1906M] Germany rejected all ceasefire proposals and remains hostile, aligned with England. England did not respond, confirming ongoing hostility. Italy reaffirmed strict western neutrality, all assets committed to Mediterranean campaigns. Russia is friendly but unable to provide direct military support due to eastern threats; passed intelligence that Turkey claims UKR→GAL, hinting at a possible split from Austria. Austria sought French cooperation against Turkey but no agreement was reached.

Support A BRE with F MAO to strengthen the Brest defense. Hold F POR as a reserve in the Atlantic. England’s coordinated assault from IRI and NAO dislodged our F MAO, cutting our Atlantic presence. Their F DEN supported Germany into Kiel, proving the Anglo-German alliance is ironclad and highly coordinated. With two units dislodged and no fleet to contest the Channel, Brest is exposed. Our defensive line holds for now, but we risk losing Kiel permanently and face a looming invasion of the mainland. Italy remains paralyzed in the Mediterranean. The only diplomatic glimmer is the Turkish push into GAL, which may distract Russia, but it won’t help us. I must retreat A RUH and F MAO to viable positions, perhaps to BUR or BRE, and urgently plead for Italian or Russian intervention, however unlikely. Russia remains friendly but cannot divert forces from the Turkish threat in Galicia and English pressure in Scandinavia. Germany and England rebuffed all offers of truce or separate peace, confirming their united hostile stance. No new agreements were reached, and France remains isolated.

Accept the likely loss of the Kiel supply center this year. All moves will avoid speculative supports and be verified for correctness.

My defensive consolidation succeeded in taking Ruhr—thanks to inexplicable German support from Kiel—but this gain is hollow without a supply center. England now holds Spain and MAO, directly threatening Brest, while their failed Picardy probe shows their intent to strangle us. Germany’s support for my attack on Ruhr is either a colossal blunder or a deliberate fracture in the Anglo-German alliance; I must urgently exploit this by offering Germany a separate peace. Italy’s move into ION is irrelevant to us. I must never again leave a key center undefended: F POR must actively contest the Atlantic. All future orders must prioritize holding Brest and Paris, and I will immediately propose a Franco-German truce to isolate England.

[S1907M] Germany rejected all peace offers and demanded surrender, confirming continued hostility. England did not respond to the revelation of Germany's prior support into Ruhr, indicating the Anglo-German alliance remains intact. Italy reaffirmed absolute western neutrality and refused any feints or naval gestures. Russia remains friendly but is pinned by Turkey and Austria, unable to provide direct assistance. No new agreements were reached; France remains isolated and must focus on pure defense.
Intent: Conduct a full defensive consolidation: move F GAS to Brest to block the expected English convoy from Wales; hold A BUR to shield Paris from Munich; hold A PIC to prevent English landings in Picardy; hold F POR to retain Portugal and avoid losing the last Atlantic foothold. No offensive moves; all orders are designed to prevent the loss of any home center this turn.

[S1907M] Phase S1907M: A catastrophic misorder. Instead of the planned defensive consolidation—F GAS to Brest, A BUR and A PIC holding—I inexplicably ordered A BUR to support A MUN to Ruhr (void) and left F GAS holding. F POR held and was dislodged by English F MAO with support from F SPA/SC; with no valid retreat, the fleet is lost. The only success: A PIC held, bouncing the English F ENG from Picardy. The Anglo-German alliance remains solid: Germany moved A HOL to Belgium with English naval support, and England tightened its Atlantic grip. My position is now dire: 3 units, 4 centers, but the Atlantic fleet is gone, leaving Brest and Gascony exposed. Italy stays neutral, Russia pinned. Lesson: Never substitute speculative supports for defensive orders; double-check all submissions. Must hold Brest and Paris at all costs, and hope for a diplomatic breakthrough.

However, I catastrophically overlooked the southern threat: England’s F SPA/SC marched unopposed into Marseilles, and F POR simply held to secure Portugal. Both centers fall, leaving France with only Paris and Brest. With three units and two centers, a disband is now inevitable. [S1901M] England agreed to a peaceful north: Norway for England, Sweden for Russia; England said he is heading to the North Sea and does not want trouble in Norway/Sweden. Germany was openly pushy, said he will move to Prussia and told me not to interfere; he never gave a clear assurance on Sweden, so assume A BER-PRU and possible northern awkwardness. Austria gave mixed signals: first floated A VIE-GAL, then agreed to a Galicia DMZ and said he would focus south; treat the DMZ as possible but not fully reliable. Turkey agreed to a Black Sea DMZ and no Armenia, says he plans Bulgaria and wants a long-term RT arrangement; warm tone but still verify by moves. Italy expects Austria/Turkey tension in the southeast and is open to information-sharing. No meaningful contact with France.
Intent: Current S1901M plan is to honor the England understanding and likely honor the Turkey understanding for now: F STP/SC-BOT for Sweden, A WAR-UKR as a southern hedge while respecting a Galicia DMZ, A MOS-STP to keep northern flexibility, F SEV H because of the Black Sea DMZ. I intend to fulfill the England Norway/Sweden arrangement. I currently intend to fulfill the Turkey Black Sea DMZ this spring, but only provisionally pending his actual move. I intend to respect a Galicia DMZ, but Austria's earlier GAL talk means I am watching closely and will react hard if he enters Galicia. Germany is not trusted; do not concede more than necessary in the north and remember he declared Prussia in advance.

[S1901M] Austria broke faith immediately by moving VIE-GAL after talking DMZ; that is the clearest betrayal and must shape all future dealings with him. Germany did exactly what he advertised and tried BER-PRU; my WAR-PRU bounce was important, both to stop him entering Prussia and to show I will not be pushed around in the north. England kept the northern understanding in spirit: no move against Sweden/Norway arrangements and no direct anti-Russian action. Turkey also honored the Black Sea/Armenia understanding this turn, which slightly improves his credibility. My own moves were more assertive than the earlier draft plan: MOS-UKR and SEV-RUM secured a strong southern foothold while BOT preserves the Sweden plan. Net result: good tactical position, but Austria in Galicia creates immediate danger to Ukraine/Rumania/Warsaw and may force an anti-Austrian response.

[F1901M] England reaffirmed the Norway-for-England, Sweden-for-Russia understanding and remains committed to a quiet north; no sign of English hostility. Germany said he will not contest Sweden this fall, but his tone stayed coercive: he demanded I withdraw from Prussia/Ukraine/Rumania and explicitly threatened coordinated pressure with Austria and Turkey, so his Sweden promise should be treated cautiously. Austria is the clearest current enemy: he already broke the Galicia DMZ in spring, then tried to excuse it as a precaution. He now says GAL will not move to WAR or UKR this turn and may move back west/defensive, but this is not trustworthy; assume any Austrian promise can be false. Turkey did honor the spring Black Sea/Armenia calm, but is now uneasy about my fleet in Rumania, says Austria and Germany are courting him, and asked for concrete concessions such as support to Greece or a Ukraine pullback; no deal was reached, and there is no firm southern agreement beyond my conditional offer of mutual non-pressure if he keeps BLA and BUL off me. Italy remains useful for information-sharing and may exploit Austrian overextension later. No meaningful contact with France. Key board memory: Austria's GAL move was the major betrayal, Germany tried PRU and was bounced, England kept the northern spirit, and Turkey was honest in spring but is now wavering.
Intent: Primary committed move is F BOT-SWE; I intend to fulfill the England understanding and secure Sweden while avoiding any move against England. I have not made any concrete concession to Turkey or Austria and do not intend to. If Germany truly leaves Sweden and the Baltic alone, I am willing to avoid a northern escalation this turn, but I do not trust him and will not concede leverage. Main operational priority is the south: preserve Rumania if possible, contain or punish Austria's Galicia army, and avoid letting GAL dictate my WAR/UKR/RUM posture. Southern orders should be defensive-first and anti-Austrian, with only conditional calm toward Turkey if he shows it by action.

[F1901M] England again proved the most reliable partner: he took Norway and left Sweden for me, so the northern understanding held and I finished 1901 on 6 centers. Germany did not contest Sweden, but his moves to Prussia and Silesia confirm he remains coercive and dangerous; any calm with him is only temporary. Austria stayed openly hostile, using Serbia and Galicia against Rumania. My A WAR-GAL was the right call: even though it bounced, it cut Austrian support and, with UKR supporting, saved Rumania. The bigger disappointment was Turkey. After earlier calm, he moved to Black Sea, sent Ankara to Armenia, and supported the Austrian attack on Rumania, showing he is now willing to join anti-Russian pressure. Main lesson: keep attacking Galicia, trust England most, and treat Austria-Turkey coordination as a real immediate threat.

[S1902M] England fully reaffirmed the Norway-for-England, Sweden-for-Russia understanding and promised no pressure on StP/SWE; this is the only firm reliable agreement and should be preserved. Italy remained cooperative, said he is preparing pressure on TRI/VIE, and wants continued intelligence-sharing against Austria. Turkey admitted Austria is pushing him into a full anti-Russian attack and asked for concrete compensation; no deal was reached. My standing offer to Turkey was simple non-hostility this spring if he does not move/support against RUM or pressure SEV from ARM, but I should assume hostility unless his moves prove otherwise. Germany was openly hostile and threatening, claiming Austria and Turkey are committed and that WAR will fall; treat Germany as an active enemy. France was receptive to information-sharing about German overextension but made no commitments. Key memory for orders: only England deal is firm; Italy is useful but not committed tactically; Turkey is probing but untrusted; Germany is explicitly hostile; Austria remains the primary southeastern enemy after the Galicia betrayal.
Intent: I intend to honor the England agreement fully this spring: no move against Norway and no northern provocation from SWE unless Germany creates an emergency. No other firm agreement binds me. I do not intend to meet Turkey's demand for concrete territorial concessions, and I do not trust his hints at a deal without visible proof on the board. Main operational intent is defensive and anti-Austrian/anti-German: assume possible coordinated pressure on WAR and RUM from Germany/Austria/Turkey, prioritize preserving Warsaw and contesting/holding Rumania as far as tactically possible, and use moves that cut enemy supports or keep Galicia from dictating the board. In the south, Austria and Turkey again coordinated hard against Rumania, and ARM cut SEV’s support as expected, but UKR-GAL successfully cut Austrian help and the Austro-Turk attacks bounced each other, so RUM survived. Main lesson: I am now facing a broad anti-Russian squeeze, and England must be reclassified from friend to opportunist.

France remains non-committal but receptive to intelligence about German eastern overcommitment; possible future diversion, no present promise. The window to stop the French juggernaut is closing; I must coordinate with Turkey and any remaining powers to open a western front before France becomes truly unstoppable.

[S1904M] France is the dominant power (8 centers) and is actively dismantling Germany. I have formed a loose coalition with Turkey, Germany, and Austria to contain the French juggernaut. Germany has requested support to retake Kiel (A BER -> KIE), which I have agreed to provide with F DEN. Turkey is finishing Russia and will then shift focus to France. Austria has proposed a naval flanking maneuver (F NAO -> IRI -> MAO) to disrupt France's Atlantic supply chain. Italy remains neutral and claims a non-aggression pact with France. France continues to maintain a facade of peace via the Channel DMZ to keep me passive.
Intent: I will break the Channel DMZ and pivot to an anti-France posture. I intend to fulfill my agreement with Germany by using F DEN to support A BER -> KIE. I will hold my northern gains (F STP -> STP, F SWE -> SWE). Following Austria's suggestion, I will move F NAO -> IRI to begin pressuring the French Atlantic flank. I will maintain defensive positions with F LON and F LVP to protect the home islands while the coalition attempts to blunt France's momentum.

[S1904M] The coalition is working. My support of Germany successfully dislodged France from Kiel, halting their momentum in the east and restoring a German buffer. I have officially broken the Channel DMZ, moving F LON to the English Channel and F NAO to Ireland, placing France on the defensive on two fronts. France's failure to react aggressively suggests they were overconfident or paralyzed by the sudden shift in alignment. Meanwhile, Turkey is systematically dismantling Russia, ensuring no northern threats emerge. However, the friction between Italy and Austria in the Ionian is a concern; I must ensure their squabbling doesn't derail the anti-French effort. My position is strong: the North is secure, the Atlantic is pressured, and France is no longer the undisputed hegemon. The goal now is to coordinate a simultaneous strike on French home centers.

[F1904M] Strong coordination with Germany to strip France of the Low Countries; agreed to support A KIE -> HOL with F DEN. Turkey is effectively eliminating Russia and shifting focus to the Mediterranean, though Turkey has stabbed Austria over Greece. Austria remains focused on France but is now actively warring with Turkey. Italy is preoccupied with the Balkan/Mediterranean conflict.
Intent: I will fulfill my agreement with Germany by using F DEN to support A KIE -> HOL. I will use F ENG and F IRI to pressure the French coast and the Mid-Atlantic to keep France pinned. F STP and F SWE will hold their respective centers to secure the North. A YOR and F LVP will maintain defensive postures to protect the home islands.

[F1904M] I successfully seized Belgium with F ENG, but I committed a critical error by ordering F DEN to hold instead of supporting Germany's move to Holland. This failure allowed France to maintain its grip on the Low Countries and successfully move into Kiel, leaving Germany crippled. My Atlantic maneuvers (F IRI and F LVP) were inexplicably bounced, stalling my pressure on the French coast. France remains the dominant power with 8 centers, though they are now forced to contend with my presence in Belgium. I must apologize to Germany and coordinate a more effective strike to dismantle the French hegemony. The lesson is clear: precise order entry is paramount; a single "Hold" where "Support" was promised can shift the balance of power.

[S1905M] Germany demands F DEN support for A BER -> KIE to restore their buffer; I have agreed to this to repair the alliance. Turkey requests help to eliminate Russia, specifically asking for a move to Moscow (which is impossible for a fleet), but I've offered F SWE -> BAL to disrupt Russian coordination. France proposed a ceasefire and a partition of Germany, which is a strategic trap and will be rejected. Austria is attempting to build an anti-Turkey coalition, creating a conflict between two of my partners.
Intent: I will fulfill my agreement with Germany by ordering F DEN to support A BER -> KIE. I will attack Holland with F BEL to strip France of a center. To assist Turkey and secure my rear, I will move F SWE -> BAL. I will maintain pressure on the French Atlantic coast with F IRI and F LVP. F STP will hold to secure the North. A WAL will move to pressure France (likely BUR or HOL). I will ignore France's offer of partition.

[S1905M] Germany successfully retook Kiel with my support, restoring their buffer and solidifying our alliance. However, my offensive against France stalled; both F BEL -> HOL and F IRI -> MAO bounced because France played an unexpectedly passive, defensive game of hold orders. While I've secured the North and repositioned to the Baltic to assist Turkey, the failure to strip France of Holland means the existential threat remains entrenched. Moving forward, I must coordinate a concentrated, multi-unit strike with Germany to break the French line in the Low Countries rather than relying on isolated attacks.

[F1905M] Coordinated with Germany to strip France of Holland (F BEL S A KIE -> HOL). Germany requested I hold Denmark to prevent French reinforcement. Turkey remains a strong ally; agreed to move F STP/NC east to distract Russia while Turkey assaults Italy in the Mediterranean. France attempted to bribe me to betray Germany, which I rejected. Italy has openly aligned with France against me.
Intent: I will fulfill my agreement with Germany by ordering F BEL S A KIE -> HOL and holding F DEN. I will move F STP/NC east (likely to GOB) to distract Russia as promised to Turkey. I will maintain maximum pressure on the French coast and heartland using F LVP, F IRI, F ENG, and A YOR to prevent France from recovering.

[F1905M] Germany and I successfully coordinated to strip France of Holland, restoring Germany's viability and weakening the French line. However, France's extreme passivity—playing hold orders across their coast—resulted in bounces at Brest and Madeira. This "turtle" strategy prevents quick gains but leaves them stagnant. My move to Botnia maintains a presence in the north to support Turkey. The voided French orders suggest a lack of coordination or desperation. I remain stable with 8 centers, but the French heartland is more resilient than expected. To break this deadlock, I must coordinate a concentrated assault with Germany on Paris and the Low Countries, as solo probes are being neutralized. France's refusal to engage actively is a sign of weakness, but their defensive posture is frustrating.

[S1906M] Coordinated a decisive strike with Germany to break France: agreed to F BEL S A HOL -> BUR and F DEN S A BER -> KIE. Turkey is aggressively dismantling Austria (UKR -> GAL) and plans to pivot to Italy; Turkey remains a strong ally. France attempted to bribe me into a truce to sow discord with Germany, which I rejected. Austria proposed an anti-Turkey coalition, which I will ignore. Russia requested I stay out of the East, which aligns with my focus on France.
Intent: I will fulfill agreements with Germany: F BEL S A HOL -> BUR and F DEN S A BER -> KIE. I will maintain maximum pressure on the French coast with F ENG, F IRI, and F NAO. A WAL will move to pressure the French heartland (likely BUR). F STP and F BOT will hold or maneuver to secure the North and maintain a presence in the Baltic as a distraction for Russia.

[S1906M] The coordinated strike with Germany was a success, effectively seizing KIE and pushing Germany into RUH. My Atlantic push also succeeded, capturing MAO and cutting French support. France continues to "turtle" in the heartland (BUR, PIC, BRE), but their perimeter is collapsing. Turkey remains a powerhouse, dismantling Austria and pressuring Italy, which keeps the southern flank secure.

My strategic position is dominant; I hold the North and have established a strong blockade of the French coast. Germany has proven to be a reliable ally. The lesson from this phase is that concentrated force—both in the Atlantic and the Low Countries—is the only way to crack the French defense. I must now coordinate with Germany to transition from perimeter pressure to a decisive strike on Paris and Burgundy.

[F1906M] Agreed to support Germany's push into Belgium (F NTH S A HOL -> BEL) in exchange for Germany taking Belgium and Burgundy while England targets Paris and Brest. Turkey is dominating the East, having captured ION and Galicia, and is now dismantling Austria. France is desperately attempting to sow discord between England and Germany, offering a separate peace and a plot to betray Germany, both of which were rejected.
Intent: I will fulfill the agreement with Germany: F NTH S A HOL -> BEL. To dismantle France, I will move F ENG -> PIC to pressure Paris, and F NAO -> POR and F MAO -> SPA to collapse their Atlantic coast. I will move A YOR -> BUR to maintain pressure on the French heartland. In the North, I will move F STP/NC -> BOT to pressure Russia, F FIN -> STP to secure the center, and F DEN -> NTH to reposition.

[F1906M] The Fall 1906M phase was a strategic mixed bag. I successfully seized SPA and secured MAO, further collapsing France's Atlantic perimeter. However, the coordinated strike with Germany was a disaster; I supported A HOL to BEL, but Germany attempted a different maneuver, leaving them vulnerable. France capitalized on this lack of coordination, using A BEL to dislodge Germany in RUH. This proves France is not merely "turtling" but is capable of opportunistic aggression. My attempt to enter PIC bounced, confirming that France's interior remains resilient. Germany is now severely weakened, which threatens the stability of our coalition. I must re-evaluate Germany's reliability and coordinate more tightly to prevent further French gains. The Atlantic is mine, but the push for Paris requires better synchronization to break the French line.

[S1907M] Germany is volatile and feels betrayed over the loss of Ruhr/Belgium in F1906M; they have demanded the return of Belgium (A HOL -> BEL) and intend to move A MUN -> BUR to attack France. I have agreed to support A HOL -> BEL to preserve the alliance. Turkey is dominating the East and requested I nudge Germany to move A MUN -> TYR to help take Vienna, but Germany's focus is currently on France. France is attempting to sow discord by claiming Germany betrayed me, which I have ignored. Italy remains focused on the East.
Intent: I will fulfill the agreement with Germany by supporting A HOL -> BEL to maintain the coalition. I will launch a coordinated strike on France: A WAL -> BUR and F ENG -> PIC to pressure Paris, while using F SPA/SC and F MAO to collapse the Atlantic coast. In the North, I will secure centers with F FIN -> STP and F SWE -> DEN, and maintain pressure on Russia with F STP/NC -> BOT.

[S1907M] The coordination with Germany was successful; supporting A HOL -> BEL restored their confidence and secured the alliance. I successfully seized POR, further dismantling France's Atlantic presence. However, the attempt to take PIC bounced, as France continues to "turtle" in their heartland. France's bizarre attempt to support a German move into RUH suggests either desperation or a clumsy ploy to sow discord.

Strategically, France is now critically weakened and isolated. My position in the North and Atlantic is secure. The primary objective remains the fall of Paris. I must ensure Germany remains committed to the assault on Burgundy and Picardy rather than drifting back into a defensive posture. The East remains volatile, but Turkey's expansion keeps the pressure off my southern flank. Focus now shifts to a synchronized final push against the French interior.

[F1907M] Agreed with Germany to support A BEL -> BUR using F NTH; Germany will not move into RUH and England will not enter BEL or KIE. Turkey is aggressively attacking Austria (targeting VIE and RUM) and requested England nudge Russia to move A WAR -> GAL, which has been done. France is desperately attempting to break the Anglo-German alliance with offers of peace and warnings of English hegemony; these are being ignored.
Intent: I will fulfill the agreement with Germany by ordering F NTH S A BEL -> BUR to help crush the French line. I will use F ENG to pressure PIC or Paris. I will secure my northern centers (STP, SWE, DEN) and attempt to seize BRE and MAR using F POR and F SPA/SC to further dismantle France. I will maintain a friendly diplomatic posture with Turkey to keep the East volatile for Austria.

[F1907M] I failed Germany by ordering F NTH H instead of supporting A BEL -> BUR, causing the attack on Burgundy to bounce. This is a severe diplomatic error I must rectify immediately to prevent the alliance from collapsing. France remains resilient in the heartland, though I successfully seized MAR, further dismantling their Atlantic presence. Turkey's surge into VIE and RUM is excellent, keeping the East volatile and my southern flank secure. The North is firmly under my control. My priority now is to apologize to Germany and coordinate a synchronized, foolproof strike on Paris and Burgundy. France is isolated and weak; they simply require a concentrated push to fall.

[S1908M] Agreed to a sphere of influence with Germany: Germany claims Paris and Burgundy, while England claims the Atlantic and North Sea. Germany requested support for A BEL -> BUR; although they mistakenly asked for F MAR (which is geographically impossible), I will provide support via F ENG to maintain the alliance. Turkey is dominating the East, crushing Austria, and moving to neutralize Italy. France is desperately offering an alliance to stop German expansion, which I will ignore.
Intent: I will fulfill the agreement with Germany by supporting A BEL -> BUR using F ENG. I will seize BRE using F POR to further dismantle France. I will hold my northern centers (STP, SWE, DEN) and maintain my positions in the Atlantic. I will continue to support Turkey's goals in the East and South to keep my flank secure.

[S1908M] France has finally collapsed. I successfully seized Brest and secured my northern centers (STP, SWE, DEN). Germany took Burgundy as agreed; although I diverted F ENG to support the move into Brest rather than supporting A BEL, Germany provided their own support from Munich, so the alliance remains intact. The "turtle" is broken, and France is now reduced to a desperate hold on Paris. In the East, Turkey remains the dominant force, though several bounces in Vienna, Serbia, and the Ionian suggest a temporary stall in their momentum. My strategic position is excellent with 10 centers and a secure perimeter. The immediate priority is the final liquidation of France and carefully managing the balance of power between my allies, Germany and Turkey, to ensure neither becomes an unstoppable threat.
